title: Active Viral Addition Enhances Terrestrial Dissolved Organic Matter Mineralization via Microbial Community Restructuring in Reservoir Water
content:
Active viral addition increased CO2 accumulation ~3.7‐fold during terrestrial dissolved organic matter mineralization in reservoir water. This coincided with a prokaryotic community shift, where Bacteroidia declined and Gammaproteobacteria enriched. Viral activity also drove molecular remodelling of DOM, reducing refractory compounds (lignin‐like, condensed aromatics) while raising labile fractions (carbohydrate‐like, protein/amino sugar‐like), thereby accelerating carbon turnover.

ABSTRACT
The role of viruses in regulating the transformation and mineralization of terrestrial dissolved organic matter (tDOM) in reservoir ecosystems remains unclear. We conducted a microcosm experiment with Three Gorges Reservoir water amended with riparian soil‐derived tDOM and different levels of active virus‐like particle (VLP) to test whether viruses regulate tDOM mineralization by reshaping prokaryotic communities and DOM molecular composition. The results show that active viral addition significantly enhanced CO2 accumulation (approximately 3.7‐fold). This was coupled with a prokaryotic community shift, characterized by a marked decrease in Bacteroidia (from 35.67% to 10.67%–16.16%) and an increase in Gammaproteobacteria (from 47.36% to 65.26%–70.08%). At the molecular level, viral addition was associated with lower double bond equivalent (DBE) and modified aromaticity index (AImod), as well as reduced relative contributions of carboxyl‐rich alicyclic molecules (CRAMs), lignin‐like, and condensed aromatic‐like compounds. In contrast, more labile fractions (e.g., carbohydrate‐like and protein/amino sugar‐like compounds) accounted for a larger share of the DOM pool. These findings demonstrate that active viral addition can enhance tDOM‐associated carbon processing in reservoir water by coupling prokaryotic community restructuring with molecular‐level DOM reworking.

title: Effects of enhanced rock weathering on soil gas fluxes across UK land uses
content:
Effects of enhanced rock weathering on soil gas fluxes across UK land uses
Kate Rees, Maria Val Martin, David Beerling, Aurelia Bezanger, Nicholas Cowan, Ruby Devlin, Mark Hanlon, Ben Langford, Sergiy Medinets, and Julia Drewer
Biogeosciences, 23, 8577–8598, https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-23-8577-2026, 2026
Enhanced rock weathering spreads crushed rock on soil to capture CO₂. We tested how this affects gases released from different UK soils in a lab study. Results varied with land uses: some soils released less CO₂ or more nitric oxide, others showed small changes in methane or other gases. This understanding of a wide range of trace gases is crucial to examine climate forcing and air quality implications of enhanced rock weathering deployment.

title: Tracing Organic Matter Dynamics Through Seasonal Cycles in Arctic Coastal Systems Using Ultrahigh Resolution Mass Spectrometry
content:
Abstract
Arctic coastal systems, including lagoons and sounds, are important zones for carbon processing and export to the Arctic Ocean, yet their role in high‐latitude carbon cycling remains understudied in comparison to rivers and the open ocean. Seasonal extremes drive dissolved organic matter (DOM) amount and composition in these systems, making the study of temporal dynamics critical for predicting climate‐change responses. In this study, we examined seasonal and salinity‐associated shifts in DOM composition in Simpson Lagoon and Stefansson Sound along the Beaufort Sea coast using Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT‐ICR MS). During the spring, greater freshwater influence was associated with aromatic, terrestrially derived DOM, whereas winter low‐flow conditions were characterized by more marine‐influenced and microbially reworked DOM, with a greater relative abundance in heteroatom content. The summer open water period exhibited intermediate conditions, with DOM reflecting a mixture of terrestrial and marine‐influenced material shaped by estuarine mixing and microbial processing. These findings indicate pronounced seasonal changes in DOM composition associated with variations in freshwater inputs, mixing behavior, and DOM processing within these coastal systems. To further characterize DOM dynamics, we identified sets of core molecular formulae that are unique and consistently observed within temporal extremes (e.g., spring and winter), representing season‐specific molecular signatures of DOM sources and processing. These seasonal signatures may serve as tracers of DOM inputs and transformations and provide a framework for evaluating how climate‐driven changes, such as longer ice‐free periods and enhanced stratification, may alter DOM composition and carbon cycling in Arctic coastal environments.

title: Variable Dimethylsulfide But Relatively Stable Isoprene Under Elevated Seawater pCO2: Evidence From Two Coastal China Mesocosm Experiments
content:
Abstract
Oceanic emissions of dimethylsulfide (DMS) and isoprene are critical to global carbon and sulfur cycles, atmospheric chemistry, and climate regulation. However, their responses to ocean acidification (OA) remain unclear. Here, we determined the impact of OA on DMS and isoprene during two mesocosm experiments in Wuyuan Bay (Southern East China Sea). Elevated pCO2 reduced DMS and its precursor, dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP), in the 2018 mesocosm experiment (spring), consistent with acid‐stress suppressing DMS(P) production by the dominant phytoplankton. In the 2019 mesocosm experiment (autumn), no significant differences were observed, likely due to community composition and species‐specific responses to OA. Isoprene concentrations remained unaffected in both experiments, indicating that its production is generally insensitive to OA. This study improves our understanding of phytoplankton‐based DMS production under simulated OA in the coastal waters of the southern East China Sea and provides the first experimental evidence of the isoprene response to OA, offering insights into how future OA may affect regional trace‐gas emissions. However, the observed concentration patterns likely reflect the combined effects of production and consumption processes, and the underlying processes warrant further investigation.

title: Parallel Modifications Across Multiple Biological Levels Induced by Urban Environments in a Freshwater Fish
content:
ABSTRACT
Urbanization drastically changes landscapes, resulting in habitat fragmentation and degradation and the loss of local biodiversity and ecosystem services. Yet, many species thrive in urban environments, with geographically separated populations showing similar responses to replicated environmental transitions over contemporary evolutionary timescales. However, little is known about the degree to which parallelism is present across multiple levels of biological organization in freshwater ecosystems. Here, we investigated three pairs of urban and rural populations of Gambusia affinis, a small‐bodied freshwater fish found abundantly across an urbanization gradient, to examine patterns of adaptive evolution across levels of biological organization. We found that morphological parallelism in response to replicated environmental transitions was underlain by both genomic and epigenomic parallelism at the genome‐wide level. However, the candidate loci and biological functions putatively associated with divergence between urban and rural populations were largely unique to individual population pairs. Finally, we found a possibly independent and complementary effect of genetic and epigenetic variation on repeated urban adaptation. Our findings suggest the complex molecular basis of rapid morphological adaptation to urban environments and provide insight into the role of contingency and determinism in adaptation to urbanization across organizational levels in freshwater ecosystems.

title: Environmental and spatial heterogeneities shape aquatic communities at tributary confluences in a desert river network
content:
Abstract
Landscape heterogeneities influence dispersal between habitats and environmental conditions within habitats, shaping the metacommunity dynamics that govern the distribution of species throughout an ecosystem. Riverine aquatic communities are sensitive to heterogeneity in flow, substrate, and other abiotic conditions arising from interactions between aquatic and terrestrial landscapes, as well as from spatial heterogeneity in river networks that can cause isolation and fragmentation. Landscape characteristics can be particularly variable at tributary confluences, where branches with different biotic and abiotic characteristics join together. Here, we investigate the effect of tributary confluences on aquatic invertebrate community connectivity in Grand Canyon, testing the competing hypotheses that (1) tributary confluences facilitate community connectivity by linking habitats and inducing gradual shifts in habitat conditions, or (2) differences in adjacent tributary and mainstem habitat conditions are sufficient to isolate tributary communities from nearby mainstem communities. Using invertebrate‐specific environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding, we quantified aquatic invertebrate community structure at 22 tributary confluences in Grand Canyon, with samples collected at the tributary mouths and in the mainstem Colorado River. We identified 667 aquatic invertebrate taxa in total, with assemblages dominated by Diptera, and tributary communities possessed higher taxonomic richness than mainstem communities. Community structure at confluences differed between tributary and mainstem habitats, with high beta diversity driven by species turnover rather than nestedness. Between tributary communities throughout Grand Canyon, beta diversity was again driven by high turnover, with environmental heterogeneity explaining more of the community structure than spatial relationships of the network. The significance of turnover at multiple scales indicates that changes in community composition are driven by local dynamics of species sorting and habitat filtering, and that ecological isolation is an important dynamic in structuring aquatic invertebrate communities. Tributaries contribute to the high aquatic invertebrate diversity in Grand Canyon, but their isolation relative to each other leaves communities vulnerable to habitat degradation and stochastic disturbances. Together, these results indicate that landscape heterogeneity at tributary–mainstem confluences limits ecological connectivity even at short geographical distances, resulting in an archipelago‐like pattern of disjunct tributary communities despite the hydrological connectivity within the river network.

title: How temperature, photoperiod, and evolutionary history shape forest leafout
content:
Abstract
Climate change has shifted the timing of major life cycle events across most systems. These shifts may in turn alter how species assemble temporally. While theory predicts that plant species should partition time to reduce resource competition—for example by leafing out at different times—few studies have examined this given the complexity of environmental cues that make timings highly variable across years and sites. Here we examine species‐ and community‐level responses in leafout across cuttings of 47 woody plant species from four sites in North America. By manipulating known temperature and photoperiod cues in controlled environments, then applying a phylogenetic Bayesian model, we estimate the effects of these cues and evolutionary history in shaping leafout across species. We found that each cue caused an advance in the day of leafout, but to varying degrees. Each of these responses, however, was highly similar across sites, exhibiting instead greater variation across species. Differences in species' responses to well‐studied temperature and photoperiod cues explained only half of the observed variation in leafout date, with the remaining variation explained in part by the estimated phylogenetic structure of leafout, representing species' shared evolutionary history. This suggests current models of leafout phenology are missing important variation that may structure species assembly within communities. Identifying these unidentified cues would improve forecasts of phenological shifts and our understanding of their effects on community dynamics.

title: Rapid evolution promotes defense‐strategy divergence in a widespread plant invader
content:
Abstract
Rapid evolution of defense strategies in non‐native plants contributes greatly to their invasion success. Many studies have evidenced reduced resistance in non‐native plants following specialist herbivore release, but how these plants adjust their defense portfolio against generalist herbivores in the introduced range remains poorly understood. Using the widespread plant invader Spartina alterniflora as a model species, we systematically compared three defense strategies against generalist herbivores—constitutive resistance, induced resistance, and tolerance—among its three genetic groups (native populations, high‐, and low‐latitude introduced populations) in a common garden. We found that compared to native populations, introduced populations as a whole exhibited enhanced constitutive resistance and reduced induced resistance, but no significant difference in tolerance. For each genetic group, native populations allocated relatively more to induced resistance and tolerance, whereas high‐ and low‐latitude introduced populations invested more in induced and constitutive resistance, respectively, despite a consistent trade‐off between induced resistance and tolerance across all groups. These findings suggest that Spartina has undergone adaptive evolution in defense strategies within just 40 years since its introduction to China, adjusting resource allocation among different strategies in response to varying herbivory pressures. Our study underscores the importance of integrating generalist herbivores and multiple defense strategies to understand the evolutionary dynamics of plant invasions.

摘要
非土著植物防御策略的快速进化对其入侵成功具有重要贡献。现有研究主要关注非土著植物在引种地响应专食性草食者压力释放而产生的抗性策略演化，却很少考虑这些植物在引入地范围内防御广食性草食者相关策略变化的全貌。我们以全球广泛入侵的禾本科植物互花米草为模式物种，通过同质园实验，系统比较了其不同遗传群组(原产地种群、高纬度和低纬度引入种群)应对广食性草食者取食的三种防御策略(组成抗性、诱导抗性和耐受性)的差异。研究发现，与原产地种群相比，整个引入种群表现出增强的组成抗性和减弱的诱导抗性，但耐受性无变化。就每个独立遗传群组防御策略投资而言，原产地种群相对偏向诱导抗性和耐受性，而高纬度和低纬度引种地种群则分别将资源更多地投资于诱导抗性和组成抗性，尽管在所有群组中诱导抗性与耐受性存在一致的权衡关系。这些发现表明，互花米草在引入中国后的短短40年内已发生了防御策略的适应性进化，通过调整不同防御策略间的资源分配来应对草食压力变化。我们的研究强调了综合考察广食性草食者和多重防御策略对理解入侵植物进化动态的重要性。

title: Host metacommunity structure drives parasite turnover at a snail's pace
content:
Abstract
Understanding how symbiotic communities assemble across landscapes remains a central challenge in ecology, particularly for parasites whose habitat is also biological. Competing hypotheses alternatively emphasize host structure, environmental gradients, or spatial processes as dominant drivers of community assembly; yet, these mechanisms remain difficult to disentangle empirically. We tested these alternative hypotheses using trematode parasites and their obligate snail hosts, a tractable system in which the ecological landscape is explicitly biological and the hosts are limited to well‐defined habitat patches. From 11,077 freshwater snails surveyed among 109 wetlands and streams in the Central Interior Highlands, we retained community data from 7577 snails and 593 infections among 63 sites. We genetically identified 21 trematode families infecting 8 host taxa. Parasite β‐diversity was dominated by turnover and was strongly predicted by host β‐diversity (Mantel r = 0.46, p < 0.001), a relationship that persisted after accounting for spatial distances, supporting a host‐driven assembly mechanism. Environmental variables, including hydrologic regime and water chemistry, influenced parasite composition primarily through their effects on host communities, consistent with habitat‐modulated host filtering rather than direct environmental control on parasites. Phylogenetic β‐diversity analyses showed that parasite lineage turnover only weakly tracked host phylogeny, placing host–parasite associated turnover closer to random than expected based on strict codiversification. Low phylogenetic turnover indicates that spatial assembly is not governed by tight coevolutionary tracking, but instead reflects the same hosts being used by distantly related parasites. We propose a host‐structured parasite metacommunity hypothesis in which cross‐trophic turnover governs spatial assembly, such that parasite biodiversity patterns emerge from host community assembly dynamics and the evolutionary codiversification history of the symbionts. More broadly, dependent communities appear to turn over at the pace of their obligate hosts, offering a general framework for symbiont ecology and cross‐trophic biodiversity scaling.

title: Hermit crabs need a conservation shell
content: Constituting over 99% of all animal species, invertebrates remain severely underrepresented in conservation research and action. Land hermit crabs (Coenobitidae) exemplify the overlooked vulnerability of invertebrates in the Anthropocene. Distributed across tropical coasts, these crabs play key ecological roles in nutrient cycling, seed dispersal, and trophic dynamics. However, they face mounting threats from global warming, habitat degradation, pollution, and the wildlife trade. Climate change disrupts their reproduction and migration, while coastal development reduces shell and habitat availability. Plastic pollution poses a particular risk, as shell‐searching behavior leads to entrapment in bottles and adoption of plastic debris as shells. In addition, wild populations are overexploited for the exotic pet trade, given that captive breeding remains unachievable or prohibitively expensive for most species. Internationally coordinated regulations are urgently needed, especially for the rarest species, to protect this unique, ecologically important, and charismatic taxon from rapid global decline.

title: Virtual influencers and the future of conservation messaging
content: Virtual influencers (VIs)—computer‐generated characters active on social media—are gaining visibility across entertainment and marketing. Yet their role in environmental communication remains understudied. We analyzed 189 VIs on Instagram and TikTok, categorizing them by persona type and assessing recent posts for sustainability content. Despite broad reach, only 16.9% of Instagram and 2.1% of TikTok accounts included environmental messaging. Using k‐means clustering with dimensionality reduction, we identified three profiles: “Low‐activity Profiles” (moderate reach, low activity), “High‐visibility Non‐advocates” (high visibility, no sustainability content), and “Sustainability Advocates” (mid‐level reach, high sustainability engagement). Despite comprising only one‐third of the sample, Sustainability Advocates produced over 90% of all environmental posts. Animal‐themed VIs, though few, were disproportionately present in this group and posted most frequently about environmental topics. We argue that these digital characters represent an untapped opportunity for conservation. Integrating Animal‐themed and mid‐level VIs into digital campaigns may increase the visibility of sustainability‐related content and represents a promising direction for future conservation communication research.

title: Beyond profiles: Supervised repeat annotation using protein embeddings
content:
by Kaiyu Qiu, Jan Ludwiczak, Andrei N. Lupas, Stanislaw Dunin-Horkawicz

Protein repeats give rise to diverse protein structures and functions, yet their sequence-based detection is often challenging because individual repeat units can diverge substantially in sequence while retaining similar structures. Most sensitive approaches rely on sequence information directly represented by alignments or derived profiles, thereby limiting flexibility and scalability. Here, we introduce TREAD (Transfer learning-based REpeat Annotation using Protein EmbeDdings), a supervised framework that reformulates repeat detection as a residue-level annotation problem and operates directly on embeddings from protein language models. Instead of constructing explicit probabilistic profiles, TREAD learns repeat-specific features implicitly, enabling residue-resolved scoring and flexible repeat segment extraction. Across complementary benchmarks based on RepeatsDB and Pfam, TREAD consistently matches or outperforms the widely used profile-based tool HMMER, particularly in low-data and high-divergence settings. The model exhibits robustness to score thresholding and demonstrates better generalization to independent test sets, including those containing remotely related families. To illustrate the practical utility of TREAD, we applied it to survey β-propeller proteins across the AlphaFold Database and representative proteomes to generate a comprehensive census of this fold. This analysis highlights extensive propeller diversity, identifies lineage-specific expansion patterns across the tree of life, and suggests previously unrecognized relationships between propellers and other repeat folds. Together, TREAD provides a flexible and scalable alternative to profile-based repeat annotation and establishes a general motif-centric framework for protein sequence annotation.

title: Vascular modelling of peripheral ischaemic disease response
content:
by Lachlan Arthur, Michele Carrabba, Paolo Madeddu, Steven McDougall, Vassilis Sboros

Ischaemic disease presents a significant challenge in medical science due to its widespread manifestations in the body and its tendency to only become overt in its late stages, beyond where current intervention methods are effective. Diseases such as coronary heart disease and peripheral artery disease (PAD) represent leading causes of death and are detrimental to quality of life. Focussing on the latter, PAD incurs an amputation rate of around 25%, largely owing to microvascular disease that prevents tissue recovery even after revascularisation. Current methods for investigating PAD either cannot chart specific vascular determinants, such as with in vivo imaging, or deform and remove subjects from longitudinal studies, such as with ex vivo tissue sampling. Presented to aid live research, computational modelling can collate information and build models of ischaemia using available information and provide a reasonable approximation of the disease’s chronology and thus support understanding and advance research of PAD. Proposed here, is a 3D in silico model of ischaemic disease in the limb using a system of purpose-built platforms. Starting with a real micro-computed tomography image of the murine hindlimb, a realistic vessel bed was generated using vascular graphing software, ViGiL. From here, the model was realised in a defined pressure gradient via flow-modelling software, numPTI. With the base model of lower limb arteries, collateral vasculature was generated throughout the vessel space. This provides a bypass system for adaptation post-ischaemia. Upon ischaemic induction, the collateral bed responds to the loss of flow and successfully adapted to recover flow with similar density and distribution of diameters in collateral arterioles (p>> 0.05). Moreover, a satisfactory flow recovery of 50% was achieved after 6 days, showing that the model can reflect the specific vascular environment in which disease is incited. The proceeds of this study lay the groundwork for truly realistic ischaemic models including moving towards a predictive model than can signify when and where key indicators of PAD manifest.

title: CoEVFold suite: User friendly pipelines to visually represent protein coevolution
content:
by Chris L. B. Graham, Liam Cremona, Robin Little, Christopher D. A. Rodrigues

Multiple sequence alignment (MSA) data underlies current principles in protein folding and protein-protein interaction prediction, from which deep-learning models trained on protein sequence and structure datasets can predict protein structure. However, what is missing are user-friendly tools that enable researchers to identify and visualise coevolution, the principal signal that these MSAs encode. Here we present tools to identify and visualize coevolution, through a pipeline (CoEVFold) that uses basic direct coupling algorithms derived from GREMLIN and an input alignment of sequences from MMseqs2. We also provide notebooks to calculate coevolution with alternative methods such as CCMpred or plmc. The pipeline generates a visual representation of coevolution for a single protein but can also represent coevolution of homomeric or heteromeric protein complexes, as well as coevolution within protein networks. The input for this pipeline can be an amino acid sequence, or protein structures from AlphaFold/RoseTTAFold, the user’s own files or the PDB. Using proteins from well-studied prokaryotic and eukaryotic model systems (Bacillus subtilis, Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae), as well as phage proteins, we show that CoEVFold detects coevolution between proteins known to interact, between protomers of known oligomers, and within known protein complexes. Benchmarked against 18 heteromeric complexes of known structure, the top-ranked inter-protein couplings identified interface contacts with a precision of 0.8 or more in 7 complexes, and CoEVMapper rankings agreed with STRING associations for an Escherichia coli cell-wall synthesis network (ROC AUC 0.72–0.74). For homo-oligomers, the top-ranked coevolution pairs not explained by the monomer structure were protomer–protomer contacts in 25% (SpoIIIE) and 47% (MlaD) of cases, against 2% or less expected by chance. The coupling calculation for a ~ 950-residue complex took 114 s with GREMLIN, compared with 116 s for CCMpred and 2,060 s for plmc. Collectively, this suite of tools, named ‘CoEVFold suite’, has broad applicability and provide a useful toolkit to those interested in dissecting protein-protein interactions and networks.

title: Deciphering the replication-division coordination in E. coli: A unified mathematical framework for systematic model comparison
content:
by Alexandre Perrin, Marie Doumic, Meriem El Karoui, Sylvie Méléard

Despite extensive research, the quantitative principles that govern the coordination between DNA replication and cell division in bacteria remain debated. Multiple theoretical models have been proposed, some postulating that a single regulatory process is sufficient to ensure replication–division coordination, while others argue that two concurrent processes are required for robust control. In this work, we develop a unifying mathematical framework within which models can be consistently formulated, qualitatively analysed and quantitatively compared. This framework also allows us to propose a new double-process model. Through theoretical analysis, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions under which single-process models can reproduce physiological cell behaviours. Beyond the correlation-based analyses extensively used to date, we further demonstrate within a comprehensive statistical framework that double-process models more accurately recapitulate experimental data across all growth conditions. Specifically, the new model we propose robustly captures the replication-division coordination in every growth regime, thereby providing a foundation for future mechanistic studies.

title: Differential vulnerability of stimulus-locked and persistent gamma oscillations: Implications in schizophrenia
content:
by Daniel W. Chung, G. Bard Ermentrout

Working memory depends on gamma oscillations generated across sensory and prefrontal cortices. In primary visual cortex (V1), stimulus-locked gamma oscillations encode stimulus information, while in prefrontal cortex (PFC), persistent gamma oscillations maintain this information after the stimulus is removed. In schizophrenia (SZ), gamma power is reduced in both V1 and PFC, consistent with deficits in sensory encoding and working memory maintenance. Both oscillation regimes arise from a canonical microcircuit involving pyramidal neurons (PNs) and parvalbumin-expressing interneurons (PVIs). Yet, whether the two regimes are similarly or differentially vulnerable to synaptic alterations within this circuit in SZ remains unknown. To investigate this question, we used a mean-field model of the PN-PVI circuit, in which the two regimes were distinguished by NMDA conductance values reflecting the difference in GluN2B expression between human PFC and V1. We then assessed three synaptic alterations quantified using molecular and structural proxies in postmortem SZ brains: lower excitatory inputs to PVIs (E→I), lower inhibitory inputs to PNs (I→E), and greater variability in E→I strength. Each alteration produced larger gamma power deficits in the persistent regime than in the stimulus-locked regime. Applied together, these alterations interacted synergistically to reduce gamma power, with the persistent regime exhibiting a more pronounced deficit. Bifurcation analyses revealed that this differential vulnerability arises from a wider margin of oscillatory stability in the stimulus-locked regime, and that reduced I→E strength additionally abolished the bistability required for the persistent regime. These findings predict that a larger magnitude of synaptic alteration is required to disrupt gamma oscillations in V1 than in PFC, consistent with postmortem reports of more severe alterations in V1 in SZ. Together, they establish a differential vulnerability model of cortical gamma oscillations in SZ, in which regional differences in oscillatory stability determine how much synaptic alteration is required to disrupt oscillations with distinct dynamics.

title: TRAFIKK: Systematic prediction and mechanistic interpretation of anticancer drug synergies
content:
by Marco Fariñas, Viviam Bermúdez, Eirini Tsirvouli, Kristine Lippestad, John Zobolas, Tero Aittokallio, Kaisa Lehti, Åsmund Flobak

Effective drug combination therapies can improve cancer treatment, yet the mechanistic basis of drug synergy remains poorly understood. Most computational approaches prioritise predictive accuracy over molecular mechanistic interpretability, providing limited insights into how synergistic effects emerge across signalling contexts. We developed Trafikk, a molecular-signalling network-based framework that simulates drug perturbations in cell-line-specific computational models to mirror functional outcomes in experimental combination screens. Across two independent large-scale datasets, Trafikk identified synergistic combinations with >77% recall. Functional response predictions revealed both conserved and context-dependent mechanisms. While AKT-MEK co-inhibition consistently disrupted coordinated survival and apoptotic signalling in 742 cell lines, PI3K-BCL2 synergy arose through distinct death programs shaped by cell-context-specific network constraints. Trafikk combines predictive performance with mechanistic interpretability, capturing how and why drug synergy emerges across cellular contexts. Source code, installation instructions and usage tutorial are freely available at https://github.com/druglogics/trafikk.

title: Correction: Single-nucleus transcriptomics of wing sexual dimorphism and scale cell specialization in sulphur butterflies
content: by Ling S. Loh, Joseph J. Hanly, Alexander Carter, Martik Chatterjee, Martina Tsimba, Donya N. Shodja, Luca Livraghi, Christopher R. Day, Robert D. Reed, W. Owen McMillan, Gregory A. Wray, Arnaud Martin

title: Distinct trajectories and predictability of individual grouping patterns in dolphins link social ageing to longevity
content:
by Kelley C. Meehan, Barbara Class, Shinichi Nakagawa, Meredith MacQueeney, Vivienne Foroughirad, Janet Mann, Celine H. Frère

Recent work has unearthed strong relationships between ageing and average sociability. Clear patterns of decreases in average sociability are observed across taxa; many of these are sex-specific. Individuals, however, generally deviate from population averages, and discounting individual variance in behaviour could disguise mechanisms of adaptation, selection, and developmental stability. Using 40 years of behavioural data from Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins, we provide new insights into social ageing. We achieve this by simultaneously measuring both mean (repeatability) and variance (predictability) in group size—a trait reflecting social interaction preference—across the population and throughout individual lifespans. Double hierarchical location-scale modelling reveals a multidimensional response; at both the population and individual level, the mean trait response (plasticity) and variance (malleability) of group size change with age. At a population level and for most individuals, average group size increases then declines in later life. This decline is more pronounced in males, though males are consistently in larger and more predictable groups than females at all life stages. Population predictability of group size increases throughout life, consistent with our prediction that social preferences strengthen with age. Individuals which are highly sociable are also highly predictable, and increased sociability and predictability both appear correlated with longevity. The positive correlation between increasing predictability and longevity leads us to hypothesise that individuals develop social competence by refining their social experiences. This process likely involves increasing social selectivity and optimising social choices to achieve a net fitness benefit. These findings provide novel insights into social ageing and illustrate how studying variance in social traits can capture processes of social competence, selectivity, and adaptation of social phenotypes occurring within an individual’s social environment.

title: Species diversity increases information flow about predation in bird communities
content:
by Agnishikhe Kumar, Jiahao Wu, Ping Ding, Jakob Bro-Jørgensen, Mylène Dutour, Ari E. Martínez, Xingfeng Si, Qiang Zhang, Eben Goodale

The Biodiversity-Ecosystem Functioning (BEF) literature has shown species diversity to be essential for ecosystem functioning and services. Yet this concept has not been extended often to behavioral ecology, so that although it is understood that acquiring social information from heterospecific individuals is an important component of ecosystem functioning, it is unclear how animal signaling at the community level, and subsequent information flow, is related to increased species diversity. Eliciting vocal responses using predator models across 10 nature reserves on a latitudinal gradient, we first show that the species diversity of birds is correlated with signaling about predation, both in the low-risk system of mobbing and in the higher-risk system of alarm calls. After finding a similar result across a fragment area gradient in one reserve, we used this system to test how interspecific information flow is affected by species diversity. Potential mechanisms behind this effect include that species are complementary in the characteristics of their mobbing calls, so more species translates into more cumulative information, or there are higher signaling rates as more individuals are involved, or a specific keystone species is more likely to occur. This experiment varied the number of species producing mobbing calls (one, two, four, eight species), with two playback construction methods (standardizing call rate, as typical for BEF experiments, or letting it increase with species richness, as in natural assemblages). Heterospecific mobbing participation (number of vocal species, number of participating individuals), and responses (call rate, probability to call in the first minute and frequency range) increased with species richness. Construction method significantly interacted with species richness, as non-standardized exemplars showed accentuated response as species richness increased. These results match expectations that complementary differences among species in the acoustic characteristics of mobbing calls, and increased call rate, both contribute to the result. There was little evidence that the signals of one particular species changed the experimental result. The overall evidence thus supports the hypothesis that the species diversity of a community is a key component influencing the quantity and the characteristics of signaling and information flow inside it.

title: Applying functional MRI analysis techniques to whole-brain calcium-imaging data to investigate structural and functional relationships in Drosophila melanogaster
content: Clarifying the relationship between structure and function is important for understanding the brain. In Drosophila melanogaster, FlyEM and FlyWire electron microscopy-based connectome data, and whole-brain calcium-imaging data are available. We applied pre-processing methods from functional magnetic resonance imaging to whole-brain calcium-imaging data and comprehensively investigated the optimal parameters. Then, we found that the FC–SC (functional and structural connectivity) correlation decreased linearly with region of interest count, and this trend was the same in flies and humans. We also developed a new, more robust method to quantify the degree of pre- and post-synaptic segregation, and investigated this in the fly whole-brain. This revealed that many neurons have unsegregated synapses. We extracted highly unsegregated synapses and compared them with random-extracted null SC matrices. Their FC–SC correlation was significantly higher, indicating that these synapses contribute to FC well. Conversely, highly segregated synapses showed significantly lower FC–SC correlation and contribute less to FC. Neurons with unsegregated synapses, like non-spiking neurons, are spread throughout the whole-brain, and they are thought to have a significant influence on FC.

title: Nitric oxide feedback to ciliary photoreceptor cells gates a UV avoidance circuit
content: Nitric oxide (NO) produced by nitric oxide synthase (NOS) is a key regulator of animal physiology. Here, we uncover a function for NO in the integration of UV exposure and the gating of a UV-avoidance circuit. We studied UV/violet avoidance mediated by brain ciliary photoreceptors (cPRCs) in larvae of the annelid Platynereis dumerilii. In the larva, NOS is expressed in interneurons (INNOS) postsynaptic to cPRCs. UV stimulation of cPRCs triggers INNOS activation and NO production. NO signals retrogradely to cPRCs to induce their sustained post-stimulus activation through an unconventional guanylate cyclase. This late activation drives ciliary beating through serotonergic ciliomotor neurons during UV avoidance. In NOS mutants, retrograde signalling, ciliary activation, and UV avoidance are defective. By mathematical modelling, we recapitulate phototransduction and circuit dynamics in wild-type and mutant larvae. Our results reveal how NO-mediated retrograde signalling gates a synaptic circuit and induces short-term memory of UV exposure to orchestrate light-avoidance behaviour.

title: Whole-soil microbial inoculation accelerates post-fire soil recovery in a mixed conifer forest
content:
Abstract
High-severity wildfires of increasing size and frequency result in the release of carbon dioxide, destroy timber resources, and reduce biodiversity, soil integrity, water quality, and recreational opportunities. Forest recovery strongly depends on the reestablishment of soil microbial communities, motivating research on how restoration of soil microbiomes in burned forests can be accelerated. Here, we used a high-intensity burn pile experiment to test the effectiveness of post-fire native soil amendment as a microbial coalescence experiment. This design enabled simultaneous and repeated sampling of unburned, burned, and inoculated burned soils while holding abiotic factors constant. All conditions were sampled at six timepoints across an annual hydrological cycle and analyzed using amplicon sequencing, genome-resolved metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and soil chemistry. Fire sharply reduced bacterial and fungal diversity in surface soils and nearly eliminated ectomycorrhizal fungi. Inoculation shifted bulk community composition toward the unburned reference state without measurably accelerating subsequent convergence. Inoculation also accelerated recovery of functions associated with nutrient cycling, especially nitrogen transformations, and introduced a diverse assemblage of mycorrhizal fungi, including genera capable of forming essential symbioses with conifers, though this signal declined over the study period. However, the introduction of host plants and the establishment of functional plant–fungal symbioses, which may prolong persistence, were not tested. Despite introducing the full diversity of soil microbes, only a subset of organisms engrafted, likely due to selection linked to pyrogenic effects. We conclude that whole-soil inoculation can shorten the dispersal-limited phase of post-fire microbial recovery, a promising step towards restoration of the soil microbiome.

title: Iron limitation reduces diatom carbon flow to bacteria through shifts in exometabolite consumption
content:
Abstract
Iron is required for photosynthesis and thus affects carbon fixation rates in widespread aquatic regions where availability is limited. Turnover of aquatic photosynthetically derived fixed carbon is largely constrained by bacterial activity, but it is unknown how algal iron limitation alters dissolved organic matter composition and subsequent processing through the microbial loop. We examined a bacterial community dependent on carbon from the diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutum to investigate how iron limitation alters bacterial carbon processing. By quantifying activity at single-cell-resolution with nanoSIMS, we found that iron limitation led to a 43% reduction in carbon-fixation but an 80% reduction in carbon transfer into bacterial biomass. Ultra-high-resolution exometabolomics revealed that iron limitation led to bacterial consumption of less labile compounds including aromatics, specific lipids, and nucleobases. A population of bacteria specific to the iron-deplete condition exhibited high anabolic activity yet low incorporation of newly fixed carbon, supporting a shift to consumption of compounds with longer residence times. From metagenome assembled genomes we identified candidate taxa and gene pathways responsible for this carbon processing shift. These results provide a mechanistic link between decreased carbon flow to bacteria under iron limitation and consumption of less labile exometabolites responsible for this decreased flow. This has implications for predicting organic matter composition and turnover in iron deplete surface oceans and manipulating algal-bacterial interactions in engineered systems.

title: Ecological and evolutionary dynamics of chlamydiae endosymbionts in social amoeba host communities
content:
Abstract
Endosymbiotic interactions have played fundamental roles in shaping the evolution of complex eukaryotes. However, how ecological processes shape endosymbioses that are still segregating in host populations have been less described. Here, we characterize the ecological and evolutionary dynamics of chlamydiae bacterial endosymbionts in dictyostelid social amoeba host communities. Our survey of over 1400 host isolates from across a 1200 km range revealed 41 unique chlamydiae haplotypes across 11 different host species, the prevalence of which significantly varied across host species and sampling locations. Patterns of chlamydiae phylogenetic divergence were not associated with geographic dissimilarity but were associated with patterns of host diversification, suggesting a shared evolutionary history and co-dispersal between some symbiont and host lineages. However, relatively few symbiont haplotypes showed both significant host specificity and high prevalence, indicating that most associations are not ecologically meaningful. Nonetheless, our laboratory passaging experiments showed that naturally occurring chlamydiae infections can be vertically transmitted across host generations. Finally, we found overall chlamydiae haplotype diversity was negatively associated with prevalence across host populations, mirroring the classic tension between selection and the influx of neutral variation due to ecological drift and stochastic environmental acquisition. To formalize this observation, we developed a stochastic differential equation model incorporating vertical and environmental symbiont transmission, as well as ecological selection and drift. This model recapitulated the observed diversity-prevalence relationship, and is consistent with a scenario in which most chlamydiae haplotypes are ecologically neutral and stochastically acquired, whereas relatively few are vertically transmitted and selectively relevant within their host populations.

title: Community composition drives metabolic competition and Staphylococcus aureus colonization resistance in synthetic nasal communities
content:
Abstract
The human nasal microbiome is a low-diversity ecosystem whose assembly principles and mechanisms of colonization resistance remain poorly understood. Staphylococcus aureus is a member of the nasal microbiome of some individuals with variable abundance. We hypothesized that nutritional competition, strain-level diversity, and nutrient availability shape community stability and the ability of commensal species to inhibit S. aureus. To test this, we constructed 50 defined synthetic communities inoculated with 5 to 10 representative human nasal bacterial species differing in strain and species composition and tracked their compositional changes across serial passages, S. aureus growth, metabolic profiles, and nutritional interactions. The resulting consortia, which assembled into communities of up to six coexisting species converged in one of three community types. Synthetic communities dominated by specific Corynebacterium propinquum strains showed exclusion of most other community members, including S. aureus. Conversely, communities lacking C. propinquum dominance showed that exclusion of S. aureus was driven primarily by a combination of Staphylococcus epidermidis and Staphylococcus lugdunensis. Growth and coculture assays showed that C. propinquum outcompetes S. aureus in conditions that resemble the nasal environment, whereas S. aureus dominates in nutrient-rich conditions. Metabolomics analyses indicated that nutritional competition, including siderophore utilization and amino acid limitation, likely underlies this colonization resistance. These results establish a reproducible and tractable synthetic community model for the human nasal microbiome and suggest that nutrient-dependent competition and microbial metabolite production are key drivers of community structure and pathogen exclusion.

title: Silicate fertilizer mitigates methane emissions from rice paddies by enriching Burkholderia to modulate microbial interactions
content:
Abstract
Rice paddies are a major source of methane emissions, and silicate fertilizer derived from blast furnace slag has emerged as an environmentally friendly amendment that reduces methane release. SF modifies the soil redox environment by supplying electron acceptors such as iron, but the microbial mechanisms underlying methane mitigation remain unclear. Here, we combined metagenomic profiling, microbial isolation, and greenhouse experiments to show that SF consistently enriched Burkholderia vietnamiensis together with methanotrophs in the rice rhizosphere. Inoculation of B. vietnamiensis strain HU01 alone reproduced the methane-suppressing effect of SF and increased methanotroph abundance. Cell-free culture supernatants of HU01 stimulated the growth of Methylococcus geothermalis and Methylocystis parvus through secreted, low-molecular-weight, heat-stable metabolites. Although metabolic modeling predicted primary metabolites such as L-glutamate and cobalamin as candidate cross-feeding factors, LC–MS/MS analysis of the highly active fractions indicated that the robust bioactivity was primarily driven by a chemically complex metabolite mixture rather than either of these compounds alone. These findings support a model in which an SF-enriched heterotrophic bacterium promotes methanotroph growth through extracellular metabolites and contributes to reduced methane emissions in rice paddies. Burkholderia vietnamiensis HU01 represents a promising microbial resource for methane mitigation and illustrates how targeted heterotroph–methanotroph interactions can be leveraged for climate-smart rice cultivation.

title: Model-guided design of defined microbial community reveals interactions underpinning plant growth and stress tolerance
content:
Abstract
Defined microbial communities (DMCs; also known as SynComs) offer a promising strategy to enhance plant growth and stress tolerance by harnessing beneficial plant-associated microbes. However, the rational design and efficient exploration of complex DMC configurations remain challenging. Here, we present an interpretable model-guided framework that integrates plant phenotyping, microbial genomics, and machine learning to optimize DMC outcomes and identify microbial interactions relevant to plant performance. Using tomato as a model, we evaluated diverse DMC, temperature, and metabolite combinations in growth experiments and used a quality-controlled dataset comprising 301 plants representing 102 DMC compositions for predictive modeling. An Elastic Net regression model trained on plant biomass data and DMC composition features enabled prediction of unseen DMC outcomes, and incorporating genomic features substantially improved predictive performance, supporting the importance of functional potential in modeling community effects. We applied the model to prioritize and design improved DMCs, which were validated in laboratory assays and field trials. One model-guided DMC significantly enhanced plant growth in the field and improved heat stress tolerance under controlled conditions. Model interpretation and multi-omics analyses highlighted specific microbial interactions, including metabolite-associated relationships involving Sphingobium sp. and tomatine, that were linked to host stress–responsive gene expression. Together, our results demonstrate a scalable framework for predicting and prioritizing DMCs and identify candidate metabolite-associated microbial interactions that may contribute to plant growth promotion and abiotic stress tolerance.

title: Liberation of galactose from lactose by gut microbial β-galactosidase prevents uterine bacterial infection
content:
Abstract
Reproductive infection is closely associated with adverse reproductive outcomes, contributing to a reduced live birth rate per pregnancy and an elevated infertility rate. Nutrition is widely acknowledged as a fundamental determinant of human and animal health, as well as the etiopathogenesis of various diseases, with the gut microbiota playing an integral part in this process. Lactose, a disaccharide present in mammalian milk, has been identified as a potential prebiotic. Here, we found that lactose was able to mitigate the inflammatory response elicited by uterine bacterial infection, preserve the integrity of the endometrial epithelial barrier, and reduce the bacterial load in the uterus. The protective effects of lactose were found to be gut microbiota-dependent and fecal microbiota transplantation from lactose-treated mice to recipient mice also ameliorated Escherichia coli–induced metritis. 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing revealed that lactose supplementation changed the gut microbiota, specifically increasing the abundance of Lactobacillus intestinalis. Whole-genome sequencing identified that L. intestinalis expressed β-galactosidase, a lactose-metabolizing enzyme. Inhibition or exogenous supplementation of β-galactosidase confirmed its essential role in mediating lactose’s protective effects against E. coli uterine infection. Furthermore, intragastric administration of [1-13Cgal]-lactose confirmed that galactose, a lactose metabolite, could translocate from the gut to the uterus. Mechanistically, galactose upregulated the CEBPB-dependent S100a8 expression after E. coli infection, and the protective effect could be blunted by S100a8 inhibition. Collectively, these findings highlight a nutrition-microbiota-host interaction that is stimulated by lactose supplementation, providing potential benefits for reproductive infection.

title: Episodic Recharge or Not? New Insights Into Aquifer Inflows
content:
Abstract
Many heavily pumped aquifers are under stress that threatens their long‐term viability, yet uncertainty about inflows hinders assessments of aquifer futures. Water‐well hydrographs can display periods of rises or diminishment of declines that are often interpreted as episodic recharge (enhanced precipitation‐driven inflows). Investigations in the High Plains aquifer (HPA), however, have found that net inflow (inflow minus outflow, excluding pumping) has been near constant for decades. These hydrograph patterns can thus frequently be explained by the relationship between pumping and net inflow with precipitation playing an indirect role. Examples from the HPA demonstrate plotting formats that differentiate between episodic recharge and unrelated episodic storage changes. Limited applications elsewhere hint at the ubiquity of temporal stability in net inflow, so more attention should be given to this phenomenon and the ramifications of misidentifying inflow mechanisms.

title: Canyon‐Trapped Topographic Rossby Waves and Their Role in Antarctic Bottom Water Formation off Cape Darnley
content:
Abstract
Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) often forms where dense shelf water (DSW) descends through submarine canyons, yet the processes governing this downslope transport remain poorly understood. We deployed a 1‐year mooring array across Wild Canyon, a major DSW pathway off Cape Darnley, a major AABW formation region. During DSW overflows, energetic 4–6‐day current oscillations developed, exhibiting strong bottom intensification and nearly in‐phase behavior across the canyon. Comparison with linear topographic Rossby wave (TRW) solutions identifies these oscillations as canyon‐trapped TRWs. Periods of energetic canyon‐trapped TRWs precisely coincide with enhanced down‐canyon flow, indicating strong coupling between the waves and DSW overflows. Increased near‐bottom stratification associated with DSW transport further strengthens the bottom‐intensified TRW structure, suggesting a positive feedback. Our results identify canyon‐trapped TRWs as an efficient mechanism linking canyons to AABW formation and suggest that canyons offshore of coastal polynyas play a key role in deep‐ocean ventilation.
