title: Timing of nutrient input pulses during ice cover regulates lake spring plankton dynamics
content:
Abstract
Rising winter temperatures can increase rain and snowmelt events, which in turn can shift the timing of nutrient runoff earlier into the winter season. Nutrients entering lakes with runoff below ice are often assumed to stay in the water column until phytoplankton growth increases in spring following increased light availability. However, bacteria are rarely limited by light, and the mismatch between winter nutrient inputs and light availability can increase lake heterotrophy following increased bacterial growth. Here, we conducted a mesocosm experiment in a mesotrophic lake (Erken, Sweden) to test the effect of nutrient input timing below ice cover across trophic levels from bacteria to zooplankton. We added inorganic nitrogen and phosphorus on two occasions during ice cover to mimic an early and a late runoff event. Bacteria assimilated nutrients independent of when they were added, whereas phytoplankton chlorophyll a concentrations were significantly higher in the late runoff scenario, likely due to a combination of sufficient light and nutrient availability. Mixotrophs increased in the early runoff scenario, likely reflecting increased nutrient availability at times of light limitation. Our findings suggest that earlier winter runoff following thaw events may result in a comparably lower spring phytoplankton bloom through changes in the timing of nutrient and light availability.

title: A segmented-breakpoint measure of cross-shore sea-surface-temperature structure in the Benguela system
content:
A segmented-breakpoint measure of cross-shore sea-surface-temperature structure in the Benguela system
Albertus J. Smit and Neville A. Sweijd
Ocean Sci., 22, 3795–3809, https://doi.org/10.5194/os-22-3795-2026, 2026
We fit a daily breakpoint to cross-shore sea-surface-temperature profiles in five Benguela upwelling cells. Conventional 50 to 100 km offshore references usually sample inside the fitted cool tongue, which can weaken or reverse fixed-distance contrasts. The method clarifies how index definition shapes cell-scale comparisons and sea-surface-temperature and wind agreement.

title: Real-world longitudinal multi-omics separates weight-loss-associated responses to incretin agonists from a broader response not dependent on weight loss
content: The benefits of incretin agonists, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists, are largely attributed to glycemic control and weight loss, as these therapies enhance insulin secretion, suppress glucagon release and delay gastric emptying to produce satiety. Yet treatment is also associated with lower risk of cardiometabolic, renal and other chronic diseases. Whether these broader benefits depend on weight loss itself or reflect direct effects of treatment on physiology remains unclear, as does the basis of the marked variation in how patients respond. Resolving these questions has been difficult because weight loss and drug effects occur together, and because molecular studies of treated patients have been limited in scope. Here we profiled paired plasma samples collected before and after treatment from 165 individuals drawn from DynamiQ, a biorepository that links plasma samples to longitudinal clinical records, combining mass spectrometry-based proteomics, a targeted inflammation proteomics panel (NULISAseq) and non-targeted metabolomics to capture metabolic function, inflammation and markers of chronic disease. Treatment was associated with broad remodeling of the plasma proteome and metabolome, but the extent to which this remodeling depended on weight loss differed across the molecular layers. The metabolome carried a lipid signature that scaled with the weight lost, whereas proteomic and inflammation-panel changes largely did not depend on weight loss. Among these changes, treatment was associated with lower circulating mitochondrial oxidative proteins and cardiolipins, consistent with relief of lipid-driven metabolic stress, and with a shift of the inflammation panel toward a less inflamed state. A metabolic aging clock showed that age acceleration decreased by a mean of 2.96 years after treatment (95% confidence interval -4.95 to -0.98; P = 3.7 x 10-3), a change that did not depend on weight loss or on the interval between samples, with the largest reductions in participants starting from the highest age acceleration, most of whom had diabetes. Treatment-associated features overlapped with features associated with cardiometabolic, renal and hepatic disease. Before treatment, higher systemic inflammation, reflecting chronic tissue stress and repair, was associated with less subsequent weight loss. Together, these findings indicate that incretin agonist treatment is associated with lower markers of metabolic and inflammatory stress and with a younger metabolic age, changes that do not depend on weight loss, identify baseline inflammation as an axis of heterogeneity in treatment response, and suggest that biorepositories linking longitudinal multi-omic profiling to clinical records can relate drug pharmacodynamics to disease risk and to variation in patient response.

title: Poxvirus-induced concurrent activation of SAMD9 and ERK establishes a unique immune state with heightened IFN-I responses to danger signals
content: Mammalian poxviruses must overcome the cellular restriction factor SAMD9 to establish productive infection. SAMD9 is a widely expressed cytoplasmic sensor of double-stranded nucleic acids (dsNA) that induces type-1 interferon (IFN-I) responses and possesses anticodon-nuclease activity targeting tRNAphe specifically. To counteract SAMD9, poxviruses have evolved dedicated antagonists, including myxoma virus (MYXV) M062, which blocks both dsNA sensing and tRNAphe-nuclease activity. However, the significance of tRNAphe depletion during poxvirus infection has remained unclear. Here, we showed that mammalian poxviruses exhibit an unexpected enrichment of phenylalanine within their proteomes and preferentially utilize UUU phenylalanine codon. In contrast, host interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) have lower phenylalanine frequencies than poxviruses and instead preferentially utilize UUC codon. Together with the known preferentially translational impairment of UUU-rich transcripts following SAMD9-mediated tRNAphe depletion, these findings suggest a mechanism by which unobstructed SAMD9 disproportionally restricts poxvirus protein synthesis while preserving host antiviral protein production. Next, using an M062-deficient MYXV mutant ({Delta}M062R), we characterized the cellular consequences of unrestricted SAMD9 activation. Unlike vaccinia virus lacking the SAMD9 antagonists C7 and K1 (VACV-{Delta}C7L/K1L), {Delta}M062R infection induced robust ERK1/2 signaling and preserved cell growth despite SAMD9 activation. Meanwhile, {Delta}M062R infection sustained expression of antiviral and proinflammatory proteins while restricting viral protein synthesis. This established a unique cellular state characterized by heightened responsiveness to subsequent innate immune stimulation. These findings identify a previously unrecognized interaction between SAMD9-mediated translation control and ERK1/2 signaling that renders a buffering effect to catastrophic SAMD9-mediated translation shutdown and thus provide new insight into antiviral restriction and innate immune regulation.

title: Two CntT methyltransferases from Actinosynnema mirum and Pseudomonas aeruginosa reveal conserved opine-type metallophore methylation but divergent biological roles
content: Opine-type metallophores have been discovered in mono- and diderm bacteria, where they allow zinc import under conditions of severe deficiency, a situation often found in natural environments. Whilst this family of metallophores is relatively well characterised, their modes of action in the organisms in which they are found remain poorly documented. In the present study, we identified and characterized two homologous SAM-dependent methyltransferases from the monoderm Actinosynnema mirum and the diderm Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteria. We showed that the corresponding AmCntT (Amir_3913) and PaCntT (PA1921) enzymes methylate their cognate opine-metallophores, staphylopine and pseudopaline, respectively. Crystal structure of AmCntT established key structural features that are unique to this family of methyltransferase, and residues putatively involved in substrate stabilization were probed by site directed mutagenesis. Further investigation showed that, unlike the staphylopine from A. mirum, which is recovered in its methylated form in the extracellular medium, pseudopaline methylation occurred only under certain stress conditions and was only detected for an intracellular pool of pseudopaline, hence suggesting a role in its degradation in P. aeruginosa. Altogether, our data revealed a new common component of the A. mirum and P. aeruginosa opine-metallophore pathways respectively involved in staphylopine and pseudopaline methylation that appears to have distinct functional implications in each organism.

title: Legionella pneumophila DenR is a bacterial S-acyltransferase for the human GTPase NRAS
content: In eukaryotic cells, the covalent attachment of palmitic acid to cysteine residues is catalyzed by the DHHC superfamily of membrane-embedded protein acyltransferases (DHHC-PAT). Here, we discovered that the bacterial pathogen Legionella pneumophila codes for its own protein acyltransferase, DenR, which hijacks host palmitoylation. Unlike the DHHC-PATs, DenR is a cytosolic protein that peripherally associates with membranes via binding of PI3P lipids through its carboxy-terminal domain. PI3P binding allosterically activates the palmitoyltransferase activity of its N-terminal circularly permuted NlpC/P60 papain-like domain, resulting in palmitoylation of the host GTPase NRAS at cysteine 181 and thereby anchoring NRAS to membranes of the Legionella-containing vacuole. Importantly, DenR-mediated S-acylation was insensitive to 2-bromopalmitate treatment, which inhibits cellular protein palmitoylation, suggesting that DenR represents a novel class of cytosolic S-acyltransferase.

title: Cryo-EM-based examinations of honey bee colony losses reveal structural insights into acute bee paralysis virus maturation and mechanical carriage
content: Honey bee colony losses pose a complex and significant agricultural problem in the United States and Europe, which has also been linked to viruses. As opposed to a purely sequence-based approach, we used cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) as an alternative sequencing- and culture-independent diagnostic tool to investigate viral pathogens associated with colony losses in the state of Texas. By purifying a limited number of viral particles directly from degraded hive remains, we could establish the identity of acute bee paralysis virus (ABPV) at the species level without prior sequencing data at 3.1 Å resolution, reconstructed of only 443 particles. We showed that small hive beetles carry mature ABPV virions, both within their digestive tract and attached to their cuticle. We successfully utilized cryo- EM to infer active ABPV replication from honey bee carcasses by reconstructing the virion structure of immature provirions at 2.35- and 2.53 [A], respectively, even several days after the collapse, despite the degradation of negative-strand RNA intermediates. Structural characterization of these immature particles revealed that ABPV capsids assemble around a condensed genomic core with the nucleic acid gradually expanding to occupy the capsid interior, ultimately bringing the VP0 structural protein in contact with VP3, which cleaves VP0 to structural proteins VP2 and 4. Together, our findings establish cryo-EM as a complementary diagnostic approach that simultaneously enables viral identification, replication-state assessment, and structural characterization, providing unprecedented insights into the maturation process of aparaviruses, a lineage of honey bee-infecting picorna-like viruses at the forefront of colony losses.

title: A simplified protocol for the generation of apical-out human bladder organoids in suspension using a rotating bioreactor
content: Bladder organoids are commonly generated in extracellular matrix domes, where apical surfaces line an enclosed central lumen, limiting experimental accessibility. Suspension-based systems have been explored to generate polarity-reversed organoids, but current models are often derived from cancer cells, remain incompletely characterized or rely on highly specialized scaffolds. Here, we describe a rapid and scalable approach to generate apical-out human bladder organoids (hBOs) from primary bladder epithelial cells using a rotating bioreactor system with minimal extracellular matrix scaffolding. Organoids form within 8 days and exhibit an apical-out phenotype with outward-facing umbrella-like cells. These apical-out hBOs tolerate 100% pooled human urine for up to 4 hours and can be infected with uropathogenic E. coli, recapitulating hallmarks of infection such as the formation of intracellular bacteria communities. Overall, the apical-out configuration enables direct access to the umbrella cell layer, thereby simplifying experimental manipulation, including infection and treatment assays under physiological conditions.

title: Understanding the dynamics of Telomerase-RNP complex in the human malaria parasite
content: Amongst the human malaria causing species, P. falciparum exhibits an interesting telomere-telomerase (TERT) dynamics. In a striking contrast to humans, which have 10-15 kb long telomeres, parasite telomeres are shorter (1-2 kb) and are maintained by a very large Pf TERT (2.5 times bigger than hTERT) and its structural RNA (Pf TR is 5 times bigger than hTR). Till date, there are no studies on Telomerase-RNP complex in the malaria parasite. The RNP complex comprises of diverged TERT and RNA-interacting proteins (Dyskerin, GAR1, NHP2, NOP10, TCAB1) and structural TR. Interestingly, Pf TR undergoes stage-dependent transcription with non-uniform (heterogeneous) transcript length. The levels of Pf TR transcripts are much higher than that of Pf TERT, suggesting that Pf TR may have scaffolding non-coding RNA roles beyond TERT function. We also observed differential expression of Pf TERT and TR-interacting RNPs with non-stoichiometric cellular abundance. These RNPs can form higher-order complexes, which can be independent of TERT and TR. Through super-resolution microscopy (STORM), we observed distinct perinuclear localization of Pf TERT in ring, trophozoite and schizonts. Genotoxic and oxidative stress conditions affected the expression and subcellular fractionation of plasmodial Telomerase-RNP complex proteins (especially GAR1, NOP10), hinting towards their probable TERT-independent roles. Immunoprecipitation of Telomerase-RNP complex revealed specific enrichment of NOP10 and HSP90, hinting towards variable binding affinities of RNP proteins to Pf TERT. Our results suggest dynamics in the Telomerase-RNP assembly may allow them to perform both canonical and non-canonical functions to support intracellular parasite survival in evolutionary distinct hosts.

title: A 6-week all-liquid caloric restriction diet reduced abundance of some butyrate-producing bacteria while increasing abundance of mucin-degrading bacteria
content: Caloric restriction diets are a common diet strategy to reduce excess weight and obesity. The diets work by lowering the number of calories or energy input below a human's normal energy expenditure creating an energy deficit. Caloric restriction diet meals can be composed of whole foods, meal replacement shakes, or a combination of the two. While the effects of these diets on human metabolism are well-known, the effects of these diets and the durability of these effects on the human gut microbiome are less well-known. The objective of this work was to investigate the effects of a 6-week all-liquid caloric restriction diet on the human gut microbiota using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to assess changes in diversity, community composition, and predicted function. We found that during the diet period beta-diversity shifts significantly away from what it was before the intervention (baseline), and returns to baseline a week after the diet. During the diet period we also observed a decrease in abundance of fiber-degrading and butyrate-producing bacteria with a simultaneous increase in abundance of mucin-degrading bacteria with a return to baseline level abundances in the post-diet period. Despite a liquid diet relatively high in carbohydrate (59% carbohydrate, 25% fat, 16% protein), predicted function analysis showed a shift in substrate preference away from dietary carbohydrates towards protein and host-glycans during the diet period. These findings suggest that despite the overall high carbohydrate content all-liquid caloric restriction diets deprive the gut microbiota of their preferred nutrient source due to the overall decline in calorie delivery which forces them to consume alternative nutrient sources like protein and host-glycans.

title: Rapid development of E. coli resistance to Bdellovibrio predation during short-term co-culture
content: When E. coli ML35 is co-cultured with Bdellovibrio sp. NC01 over 72 hours, prey populations initially experience a 3-log reduction, but then partially recover to ~20% of starting density. Population recovery is correlated with emergence of irregular colonies, which are distinct from typical circular ML35 morphotype. ML35 populations do not recover when co-cultured with Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus HD100, and irregular colonies are not observed in HD100 co-cultures or in prey-only controls. Whole-genome sequencing of clonal lines of irregular and circular morphotypes from three independent replicate assays confirmed they are derived from ML35. ML35-irregular is resistant to killing by Bdellovibrio sp. NC01 but susceptible to killing by HD100, indicating strain-specific predation resistance. Analysis of sequencing data showed that all three ML35-irregular lines and all three ML35-circular lines carry a mutation in rfbG, annotated as dTDP-rhamnosyl transferase involved in O-antigen synthesis. Two ML35-irregular lines have distinct IS element insertions in rfbG; the third has a substitution introducing a premature stop codon near the C-terminus. Two ML35-circular lines have the same missense mutation in rfbG, whereas the third has a nonstop mutation. Overall, these data suggest that rfbG may be under selective pressure during NC01 co-culture and that O-antigen may play a role in predation resistance. Further work, such as phenotypic testing of ML35-circular lines and reverse genetics experiments, are needed to clarify how rfbG affects prey susceptibility to Bdellovibrio predation.

title: Characterizing the Effects of Filtration on Microbial Diversity, Reproducibility, and Genome Recovery from Wastewater
content: Filtration is widely used in wastewater microbiome workflows, but how pore size, filtration tactics, and sampled fraction shape microbial profiles across sequencing approaches remains unclear. We compared direct and sequential filtration of wastewater through 3-, 0.45-, and 0.22- micro meter filters and analyzed filter-retained and corresponding filtrates using 16S rRNA gene and ITS amplicon sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and metatranscriptomics. Filtrates generally yielded higher microbial alpha diversity but greater between-replicate variability, whereas filters produced more reproducible bacterial DNA profiles. Fraction-dependent differences were strongest for fungal and DNA viral communities, which separated between filters and filtrates, while bacterial DNA communities were largely shared across fractions. These patterns demonstrate that pore size does not act as a strict size cutoff in wastewater for bacteria. DNA viruses were consistently enriched in filtrates, which also yielded more viral genomes. In contrast, filters yielded more bacterial metagenome-assembled genomes, but overall bacterial genome recovery was limited. Bacterial and viral metatranscriptomic profiles were comparatively variable and did not support selection of a single preferred fraction for RNA-based recovery. Direct and sequential filtration also produced distinct profiles at the same terminal pore size, indicating that filtration history influences the recovered community. Together, these results suggest that wastewater processing workflow should therefore be selected according to the intended use case.

title: A multi-scale forecasting framework to prioritize clinically-relevant antibiotic resistance alleles
content: Established in vitro measures for the emergence of antimicrobial resistance, a critical global threat, can fail to predict which in vitro discovered mutations will dominate in the real world following widespread antibiotic use. Here, we introduce a multi-scale computational framework integrating genetic constraints and population pharmacokinetics and apply it to explain resistance allele success in Acinetobacter baumannii for the historic case of resistance to the fluoroquinolone antibiotic ciprofloxacin. By coupling intrinsic nucleotide substitution likelihoods with continuous-time stochastic modeling under fluctuating drug exposures, our framework clearly prioritizes the most common real world gyrA fluoroquinolone resistance allele S81L over rarer alleles, reflecting its clinical success. While gyrA serves as a proof-of-concept case study for direct, active-site drug-target interactions where the target space is constrained, we observe that the nucleotide substitution likelihoods are not explaining allele success in resistance-determining genes pmrB and adeS. Furthermore, "virtual twin" cohort simulations reveal that restricted drug penetration or compromised immunity expands selective windows, rescuing rare, low-fitness alleles. This advances our understanding of prospective, model-informed risk prediction during antibiotic development.

title: Klebsiella taiwanensis sp. nov., and Pseudomonas ficus sp. nov., novel taxa isolated from figs (Ficus)
content: Two bacterial strains, WOUb02T and WOUb67T, were isolated from fresh figs (Ficus spp.) collected from the island of Taiwan. Cells of WOUb02T and WOUb67T were Gram-stain-negative rods. Strain WOUb02T was non-motile, whereas WOUb67T exhibited motility. Physiologically, both strains grew optimally at 0.5% (w/v) NaCl and pH 8.0; WOUb02T grew optimally at 37{degrees}C, whereas WOUb67T grew optimally at 30{degrees}C. Based on 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity, the closest relatives to strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T were Klebsiella terrigena ATCC 33257T (98.2%) and Pseudomonas putida NBRC 14164T (99.9%) respectively. Subsequent phylogenetic analysis based on 16S rRNA gene sequences revealed that strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T formed distinct lineages within the genera Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, respectively. Further genomic analyses revealed that WOUb02T and WOUb67T shared average nucleotide identity and digital DNA-DNA hybridization values <95.0% and <70.0%, below the currently accepted thresholds for species-level delineation. Based on phenotypic and genotypic data, strains WOUb02T and WOUb67T could be distinguished from other species with validly published names and are considered to represent novel species in the genera Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, respectively, for which the names Klebsiella taiwanensis sp. nov., and Pseudomonas ficus sp. nov., are proposed. The type strains are WOUb02T (=NRRL-B 65719T =CCUG 77855T) and WOUb67T (=NRRL-B 65720T =CCUG 77856T).

title: Species turnover dominates plant trait variation along continental climate gradients
content: Variation in plant functional traits along climate gradients chiefly arises from two processes: turnover of species with different trait values, and trait adjustment within species across environments. Yet, the relative contributions of these processes remain poorly quantified, limiting our ability to predict how traits, species distributions and, in turn, ecosystem properties will respond to climate change. Across seven functional traits and 1867 plant taxa from continental Australia, we provide a unified assessment of among- versus within-species contributions across multiple dimensions of plant function. Species turnover emerged as the dominant process driving trait variation along both precipitation and temperature gradients. Nevertheless, the contribution of within-species adjustment to climate differed substantially among traits and was generally greater in non-woody than woody taxa, these patterns being most clearly expressed along precipitation gradients. Our findings imply that plant traits will track changing climatic conditions primarily through species replacement, particularly for traits such as wood density and seed mass. Species may also respond in situ through adjustments in leaf physiology and morphology and, in woody taxa, through shifts in relative allocation between leaves and stem tissues. This knowledge has potential to improve predictions of the structure and function of future plant communities.

title: Historical overestimated abundance of a Critically Endangered species: the case of the tamaraw (Bubalus mindorensis) of Mindoro Island
content: Population abundance is a central parameter in conservation, for which biased estimates can seriously undermine management strategies for threatened species. The tamaraw (Bubalus mindorensis) is a Critically Endangered large herbivore endemic to Mindoro Island, Philippines. The species has been monitored annually at Mounts Iglit-Baco Natural Park (MIBNP) since 2000 using a multi-vantage-point count method that is prone to both imperfect detection and repeated counting of the same individuals across sessions. Because the historical abundance estimation is an index of relative abundance with no probabilistic modeling of counts, the actual number of tamaraw in what is considered as the largest remaining population is still poorly known. To fill this gap, we conducted an independent double-observer experiment over five years (2022-2026) and fitted Bayesian hierarchical detection models to the counts. As expected, detection probability was <1 throughout (single-observer estimates 0.41-0.84; combined-observer 0.68-0.96), confirming that a substantial fraction of animals is missed by rangers during all counts. Compared with these estimates, historical counts overestimated tamaraw abundance by a factor of 1.61-2.34, yielding a mean population size across 2022-2026 of 203 individuals (95% credible interval 182-226) rather than the roughly 400-500 individuals previously assumed. Our results imply that the MIBNP tamaraw population, while more vulnerable to demographic and genetic risks than previously believed, has likely responded positively to ongoing conservation efforts; we recommend that population viability assessments and translocation plans for the species be revised accordingly.

title: Apple floral attractants function across the 24-hour cycle to support potential diurnal and nocturnal pollinators
content: Pollination in apple (Malus domestica Borkh.) is typically attributed to diurnal bees, yet nocturnal insects also contribute to fruit set. To assess whether apple flowers recruit potential pollinators throughout the 24-hour cycle, we quantified diel patterns in floral attractants and insect visitation in an orchard in Northwest Arkansas, United States. We measured nectar and volatiles and used a combination of visual surveys, light traps, and video recordings to assess insect abundance and floral visitation while controlling for weather conditions. We found that nectar volume remained consistent across sampling times, indicating that reward availability is dielly stable. Floral volatile bouquets, in contrast, exhibited subtle but significant diel and interannual variation, driven largely by shifts in aldehydes, alkanes, and benzenoids. Several compounds associated with nocturnal moth and dipteran attraction - including alpha-farnesene, benzyl alcohol, and aldehydes - were enriched at night. Apple flowers were visited by insects around the clock. Nighttime visitors were less abundant than daytime visitors but taxonomically diverse, including moths and nematoceran flies, whereas bees, wasps, and brachyceran flies were restricted to daytime. Different taxonomic groups therefore alternated over the diel cycle, producing pronounced shifts in visitor community composition. Thus, apple flowers produce attractants across the diel cycle and nocturnal insects - particularly dipterans and moths - are a consistent, ecologically meaningful component of the apple flower-visiting assemblage. Our findings support the need for pollinator-inclusive management that accounts for the full diel cycle, particularly when scheduling pesticide applications near bloom, to sustain diverse pollinator communities and enhance the resilience of apple production systems.

title: The use of cultured symbionts enhances the survival of reef-deployed coral recruits
content: Introduction: Symbiodiniaceae dinoflagellates are essential for coral juvenile development and survival, yet early-life symbiont provisioning remains underused in coral restoration. Objectives: We tested whether inoculating sexually propagated Acropora spathulata recruits with cultured symbionts before reef deployment improves survival and shapes symbiont community composition. Methods: Recruits inoculated with cultured Cladocopium sp. (C1) or Durusdinium trenchii (D1), and uninoculated recruits (Control) were deployed on the central Great Barrier Reef. Results: Both inoculation treatments approximately doubled survival relative to Control, although the benefit varied with local benthic habitat. C1 and D1 recruits were dominated by symbiont sequences matching their respective inoculated cultures, while Control recruits predominantly harboured a Durusdinium-dominant community closely resembling the cultured D1. Cultured C1 was also dominant among most C1-inoculated recruits after nine months, although some diverged from the inoculated community towards a mixed assemblage with Durusdinium. Conclusions: Similar survival benefits in the two inoculation treatments suggest that the timing and success of symbiont establishment were more critical for early survival than symbiont genus identity, under the conditions and period of this study.

title: Differential population declines across migratory strategies are shifting European bird communities towards residency
content: Previous studies revealed steep declines in populations of common migratory birds across Europe, especially for long-distance migrants. However, these studies focussed on continental-scale patterns, and they assigned a single migratory strategy to each species, often not distinguishing short-distance migrants from residents. It thus remains unclear whether the same patterns are found across European countries, and whether they hold when taking into account the variation in migratory behaviour observed across the European populations of many species. Here, we examine how European breeding landbird communities have varied according to migratory strategy between 1990 and 2023, at both continental and national scales. By compiling multiple sources of information on seasonal movements, we characterise the migratory strategy of landbird populations per country (long-distance migrant, short-distance migrant or resident). We combined these data with estimates of population trends and of abundance from national monitoring schemes to quantify changes in both multi-species indices (average change across species) and total abundance of birds, for each migratory strategy. At the continental scale, multi-species indices reveal a strong decline in long-distance migrants (-26.8% between 1990 and 2023), whereas short-distance migrants declined more slowly (-4.5%) and residents remained stable. Changes in total abundance show even steeper declines - of 29.9% and 10.2% for, respectively, long- and short-distance migrants - whereas residents increased slightly (+3.4%). Together, these results point to a gradual reorganisation of bird communities towards a greater dominance of resident birds across Europe. However, these changes are not happening homogenously across the continent: whereas in Central and Southern Europe we observed the same general pattern of declining migrants while residents remained broadly stable or increased, in Northern Europe we reveal declines for all migratory strategies. Overall, our study highlights the widespread vulnerability of migratory birds in Europe, while showing that the reorganisation of bird communities follows different trajectories across regions.

title: Normalised whole-plant water supply declines with plant height across the seed-plant phylogeny
content: Whole-plant water-transport capacity largely controls terrestrial water fluxes, yet it is unresolved to what extent its variation across the seed-plant phylogeny is structured by shared ancestry, edaphoclimatic conditions, plant height or water relation traits. We fitted a phylogenetic structural equation model to maximum leaf-specific whole-plant hydraulic conductance (kL), together with concurrent Huber value (Hv), stomatal conductance (gs), and height for 263 species spanning the global climate space, partitioning direct from indirect effects, and phylogenetically conserved from independent effects. kL declined with height, and Hv did not offset this decline. Hv raised kL but was unrelated to height among species. kL was lower in wetter niches, despite higher Hv there, indicating lower conductance per unit sapwood area. kL was tightly coupled to gs in both conserved and independent variation, so the height-driven decline in kL propagated to gas exchange. Plant height therefore constrains whole-plant hydraulic supply and, through it, gs.

title: Burn Severity Shapes Post‐Fire Methane Uptake in European Boreal Forest Soils
content:
Abstract
Forest fires are increasing in frequency and severity across boreal regions, yet their long‐term impact on soil methane (CH4) fluxes remains uncertain. Understanding the conditions that govern post‐fire CH4 dynamics is critical for projecting fire‐climate feedbacks in northern forest ecosystems. Fire severity alters soil microclimate, organic horizons, physiochemistry, and microbial function, yet severity‐resolved evidence from European boreal forests remains scarce. We measured CH4 fluxes over 28 months following prescribed burns in Scots pine‐dominated forests in Finland. Fire severity, quantified via field assessments and remote sensing, emerged as a key driver of post‐fire CH4 uptake. Low‐severity burns had greater CH4 uptake than unburned areas, resulting in an estimated 46% higher cumulative uptake over the first two growing seasons. In contrast, uptake in higher‐severity burns was comparable to that in unburned areas. Maximum uptake occurred after approximately 0.3–0.4 cm of organic‐horizon consumption, consistent with improved gas transport following limited removal of the surface organic layer, whereas uptake declined with greater organic‐horizon consumption. Across the severity gradient, warmer and drier soils increased CH4 uptake. Hierarchical partitioning showed that soil moisture and temperature together accounted for 81.5% of the variance explained by model predictors, whereas residual organic‐horizon depth and canopy mortality accounted for 17% and time since fire for 1.5%. Our findings demonstrate that post‐fire CH4 uptake depends on fire severity and associated soil environmental conditions rather than on fire occurrence alone. Accounting for fire severity and soil environmental responses should improve predictions of post‐fire CH4 dynamics in boreal ecosystems.

title: Eight Unique, Novel Pseudoxanthomonas and Pseudomonas Bacteriophages Provide First Insight Into the Viral Ecology of Agaricus bisporus Mushroom Compost
content:
The microbes in mushroom compost are essential for button mushroom production, especially nitrifiers such as Pseudoxanthomonas. We report eight diverse and novel bacteriophages from compost, belonging to five new genera, which are stable at high temperatures and use Pseudoxanthomonas and Pseudomonas spp. as hosts.

ABSTRACT
Button mushrooms (Agaricus bisporus) are cultivated commercially on a specialised compost prepared mainly from wheat straw and poultry manure, which is selective for growth of Agaricus. During composting, a succession of bacterial communities transform these substrates into productive compost and reach a stable, climax community dominated by Pseudoxanthomonas. These bacterial dynamics have been well studied, but the presence and role of bacteriophages in mushroom compost is unknown. Here, we report the first observations of eight novel, genomically diverse bacteriophages isolated from mushroom compost. These include four phages infecting Pseudoxanthomonas taiwanensis, three infecting Pseudoxanthomonas suwonensis and one Pseudomonas aeruginosa phage belonging to genus Yuavirus. The isolated phages are morphologically diverse, spanning siphovirus, podovirus and Inoviridae morphotypes. They are stable at high temperatures and their genomes share little resemblance to known phage genomes, with the Pseudoxanthomonas phages belonging to five new genera. The novelty of these phages provides new insights into phage diversity and contributes to a broader understanding of the overall microbial community within mushroom compost. Their interactions with their bacterial hosts have implications for the growth of button mushrooms and this study provides a foundational starting point for investigating the function of bacteriophages in the mushroom composting process.

title: Gross primary productivity of forest ecosystems in a subtropical city and its decadal climatic and environmental drivers
content:
Gross primary productivity of forest ecosystems in a subtropical city and its decadal climatic and environmental drivers
Hayden C. H. Lam, David H. Y. Yung, Donald K. C. Tao, Joshua T. W. Lo, Man Sing Wong, Jin Wu, and Amos P. K. Tai
Biogeosciences, 23, 8599–8616, https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-23-8599-2026, 2026
We studied how forests in Hong Kong take up carbon through plant growth between 2002 and 2018. Using computer models, we found that forests remove a small but indispensable share of the city’s carbon emissions, mainly driven by changes in leaf area. This shows that forest management strategies can support climate goals, and highlights the role of local forests in working toward carbon neutrality targets.

title: Ideal foragers react to risk, not food
content:
Abstract
Organisms facing trade‐offs between food and safety in heterogeneous environments can optimize their outcomes by choosing where to live, when to be active, and when and where to forage. Numerous studies providing foraging opportunities in ostensibly safe versus risky patches reveal the inevitable trade‐offs among these activities. Very few do so while simultaneously accounting for density‐dependent habitat selection. I address this fundamental gap in experimental design by providing meadow voles free opportunities to occupy one of two identical habitats with and without experimental manipulation. The two‐phase experiment sequentially reduced the supply of commercial rabbit chow available to voles, then varied the safety within interconnected enclosures. Population density, foraging in safe and risky patches, incidental predation on alternative food sources, and food consumption were quantified during each treatment period. Vole densities quickly attained a stable and equal distribution between enclosures that was also maintained during juvenile recruitment. Analyses with repeated measures revealed consistently higher giving‐up densities (GUDs) in risky patches than in safe ones, but no other statistically significant effect of food reduction. The reaction to reduced safety was different. Voles retained higher GUDs in risky patches where they also consumed less supplemental food. Both effects varied with the time course of treatments that first reduced safety in one enclosure before repeating the manipulation in the second. Incidental predation increased through time with increased population density. The research reveals a mosaic of reactions to risk that integrate density‐dependent habitat selection with optimal decisions on patch choice. The results thus confirm the expectation that, over relatively short periods of time, foragers deem an increase in risk as more hazardous than a reduction in the availability of food.

title: Scale‐dependent support for the Stress Gradient Hypothesis using a negligible effects approach in dune ecosystems
content:
Abstract
Ecological theory can inform the restoration and preservation of imperiled ecosystems. The Stress Gradient Hypothesis (SGH) posits that community assembly rules shift from competitive to facilitative as environmental stress increases. Neutral Theory offers a null hypothesis for community assembly wherein communities assemble due to stochasticity, competitive equivalence, dispersal, and drift. Testing the relative importance of these theories in an ecosystem that exhibits a clear and stark environmental stress gradient is ideal. Coastal dune ecosystems are well‐suited to study community assembly theories because they exhibit a consistent stress gradient within and between sites. Environmental stressors—such as wind abrasion, salinity, lack of nutrients, water stress, and others—all sharply decline with increased distance from the ocean over a relatively short distance. In this study, we tested two commonly applied community assembly theories (the SGH and Neutral Theory) in three California dune ecosystems using a nested plot design, community dissimilarity as a proxy for whether facilitative or competitive dynamics were dominating assembly rules, and a negligible effects framework. At the smaller, within‐plot level, we found that most environmental factors did not impact community dissimilarity but adhered closely to the predictions of the SGH with soil salinity. At this scale, however, we showed that community dissimilarity does not align with either the predictions of the SGH or of Neutral Theory along soil temperature gradients. At the larger, between‐plot scale, we demonstrated that, while neutral dynamics (spatial autocorrelation) has a significant but negligible effect, community dissimilarity is largely driven by environmental niches (environmental dissimilarity). Ultimately, this study provides evidence for the SGH and improves our understanding of plant community assembly in dunes and other stressful habitats, which can be used to better protect and restore these imperiled ecosystems.

title: Anatomical anomalies: Morphological and performance impacts of limb loss in the Italian wall lizard (Podarcis siculus)
Vultures stabilize carrion decomposition rates during mass mortality events
content:
Abstract
Prior research emphasizes the demographic consequences of mass mortality events (MMEs), but effects on ecosystem services like carrion decomposition remain underexplored. We designed two experiments using donated wild pig (Sus scrofa) carcasses to test two hypotheses: (1) MMEs increase future carrion decomposition rates by elevating necrophagous fly abundance, but (2) vultures (i.e., Cathartes aura, Coragyps atratus) suppress fly response and subsequent decomposition rates. First, we crossed five levels of carrion biomass (25, 60, 180, 360, 725 kg) with vulture access (10 total plots). Blow fly abundance increased with carrion biomass, but vulture access halved the slope of this relationship. After 17 days of active decomposition, we initiated a second experiment. We exposed six additional carcasses (20–25 kg) for 4 h to low (25 kg), medium (180 kg), and high (725 kg) carrion biomass, again crossing with vulture exclusion. Then, we relocated these additional carcasses to a common garden and measured decomposition rate over 4 days. Decomposition rate for the additional carcasses increased with initial carrion biomass exposure, but vulture access reduced the slope of this relationship by 41%. Our results demonstrate that vultures provide ecosystem resistance by suppressing fly abundance and slowing carrion decomposition after spatiotemporally concentrated carcass inputs.

title: Participatory science reveals novel songbird–flower interactions
content:
Abstract
Songbirds are overlooked as flower foragers and potential pollinators across much of North America. We reviewed >100,000 iNaturalist observations to assess songbird–flower interactions and explore floral traits as a predictor of centrality in foraging networks. We identified 328 flower foraging observations, including 49 previously unreported interactions between songbird families and plant genera, 44 nectar robbing events, and 1420 pollen horns. Orange‐crowned Warblers and Hooded Orioles flower‐foraged and nectar‐robbed most often, and robbery primarily occurred on long‐tubed flowers. Plants most central to foraging networks were ornamentals, which could reflect availability in urban areas or photographer preference, yet songbirds also visited 17 native species. Floral traits, especially red flowers, were associated with network centrality. Our findings suggest that flower foraging by songbirds in North America has been underestimated, with implications for pollen transport and conservation. Our data show the untapped potential of participatory science to expand our understanding of species interactions.

title: Plant diversity, intermediate disturbance, and ecosystem services of small mammals in an early grassland succession
content:
Abstract
An intermediate level of disturbance (ID) is considered to promote the greatest biodiversity in communities, as both competitive and colonizing species can coexist. This intermediate disturbance hypothesis (IDH) has been controversial, in part because living disturbance agents are often also consumers, which entangles consumption and disturbance effects. We studied the impact of a graminivorous (consuming) and semi‐fossorial (disturbing) small rodent, the common vole Microtus arvalis, over a 5‐year grassland succession using a replicated experiment with 16 enclosed, sown grassland plots of 2.4 m2 (96 plant surveys). Eight plots received annual vole additions over 13 ± 12 days, mimicking high autumn densities of fluctuating rodent populations (disturbed), while the other eight plots remained undisturbed. We studied (1) combined consumptive and disturbance effects, and (2) a gradient of disturbance under controlled consumption to test the IFD. We measured diversity of different functional plant groups, vegetation structure, and the provisioning service of the grassland. Disturbance affected the succession processes and shifted the vegetation composition, decreasing vegetation cover, and facilitating persistence of rare, flowering, and ruderal plants, which had declined over time in undisturbed plots. While local plant diversity was not affected, regional γ‐diversity of joint disturbed plots and differentiation among disturbed plots (β‐diversity) was doubled, compared to the joint undisturbed plots. Vole activity decreased agricultural fodder value of the grassland. Individual voles varied in digging activity. We analyzed disturbance (as volumes of disturbed soil) as a gradient in disturbance intensity. Intermediate disturbance levels in autumn decreased the annual turnover rate of plant species during succession and promoted higher plant richness in the following summer, while both low and high disturbance levels reduced diversity and increased turnover. Through burrowing and selective foraging by voles, disturbance facilitated a higher plant diversity by maintaining rare and flowering plants, disrupting the successional pattern. Thus, a species often regarded as a pest can also function as an ecosystem engineer. Burrowing and soil movement supported plant richness best at intermediate levels, supporting predictions of the IDH.

title: Warming decreases and dominant species removal increases subdominant plant biomass consistently across a growing season
content:
Abstract
Global warming and dominant plant species influence plant biomass, a key component of the carbon cycle. Warming often has seasonal effects on biomass, shifting production earlier in the season, but it is unclear how biotic interactions will affect these seasonal dynamics. To determine the interactive effects of warming and dominant species on plant biomass across a growing season, we used a warming and dominant species removal factorial experiment established in 2013 at a low‐ and high‐elevation meadow. We measured biomass weekly throughout the 2022 growing season and calculated rates of change in biomass between consecutive sampling periods. Independent of elevation, subdominant biomass was consistently higher with dominant species removal and lower with warming, with no significant interaction. Forb biomass was lower and shrub biomass tended to be lower in warmed plots, and graminoid biomass was higher in dominant species removal plots. Subdominant biomass differed among the treatments early in the season, and these differences were maintained throughout the season, as there was no subsequent difference in biomass accumulation rates among treatments throughout the growing season. This suggests that early‐season biomass differences may regulate total biomass accumulation over the season. Our findings highlight surprisingly consistent plant biomass responses to warming and dominant species removal across the growing season and between elevations in montane ecosystems, providing context for understanding their combined effect on carbon cycling.

title: Cascading negative feedbacks stemming from marine heatwaves erode coral reef resilience
content:
Abstract
The southern Great Barrier Reef (GBR) was exposed to unprecedented thermal stress in 2024 during the world's fourth global coral bleaching event (GCBE4). The thermal conditions experienced by corals are spatially and temporally heterogeneous, and daily exposure to local temperature variability can increase the thermal tolerance of reef‐building corals. Yet, it remains unclear whether life‐long acclimatization to temperature variability, and the elevated thermal tolerance this leads to, can protect corals during extreme heatwaves. To address this question, we collected 10 years of in situ temperature and benthic cover data (2015–2024) across eight sites varying in diel temperature fluctuations (2.4–7.7°C day−1) at Heron Island, southern GBR. These data encompass two marine heatwaves (2020 and 2024) and revealed changes in coral community composition and widespread declines in coral cover and reef rugosity. Approximately half of all hard coral was lost during the decade‐long study. However, declines in hard coral cover were greatest within thermally variable habitats. Although heat stress accumulation was similar across habitats during both marine heatwaves, thermally variable habitats experienced substantially greater coral loss, with live hard coral declining by 66%–82% on the reef flat and deep lagoon compared to 35%–39% on the reef slope. Changes in community composition were site‐specific, with a functional extinction of Seriatopora and Stylophora observed in the lagoon, and significant declines in tabulate/corymbose/digitate and plating/encrusting acroporids (including Montipora) on the slope by 2024. A few months after the 2024 heatwave, many coral species were exhibiting signs of disease (e.g., white syndrome) and skeletal growth anomalies for the first time in the 10‐year study, highlighting the cascading effects of heat stress. The most structurally complex reef slope sites had not yet experienced severe declines in reef rugosity several months after the 2024 heatwave, and skeletons of dead corals remained intact for up to 4 years, providing settlement substrate for coral recruits. These results highlight the benefit of long‐term monitoring in revealing the complexity of community responses across environmental mosaics and underscore that priming to variable thermal regimes does not safeguard against mortality during marine heatwaves.

title: A discovery of emergent drivers pipeline uncovers parameter hierarchies in spatiotemporal agent-based tumor models
content:
by Po-Hao Chiu, Jacob I. Evarts, Jason Y. Cain, Neda Bagheri

Tumor heterogeneity is a confounding factor that stems from individual cell decisions, regulation among diverse cells, and regulation between these cells and the tumor microenvironment. Identifying cellular and microenvironmental factors that drive tumor heterogeneity is critical to effective therapeutic targeting. However, current experimental methods to uncover the drivers of such heterogeneity can obscure the relative contributions of the microenvironment and cell-intrinsic properties. Similarly, standard parameter estimation methods for spatiotemporal models do not rank parameter importance or resolve equifinality, the property by which different parameter combinations yield equivalent emergent behaviors. Here, we introduce a likelihood-free discovery of emergent drivers pipeline to uncover combinations of parameter distributions that lead to observed emergent tissue dynamics and compare parameter–output dependence among equifinal fitted regions. This pipeline couples approximate Bayesian computation with sequential Monte Carlo and distributed random forests to fit target metrics and characterize these associations within spatiotemporal agent-based models. Mutual information analysis compares these dependence profiles among regions. We leverage correlations among the gen-4 particles to reduce the parameter search space via pairwise linear regression substitution and hierarchical clustering-based grouping without degrading fit to emergent target metrics. When applied to breast cancer data, the pipeline identifies separated fitted parameter regions that reproduce similar target metrics and exhibit different parameter–output dependence profiles. These findings identify candidate parameter relationships for direct tests of mechanistic redundancy.

title: Generating scRNA-seq data from bulk RNA-seq using a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder
content:
by Myles Kim, Corey M. Williams, Guangzhi Xiong, Hyun Jae Cho, Steven Siadaty, Eric Xie, Aidong Zhang, Stefan Bekiranov

Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) provides detailed, genome-wide gene expression profiles at single-cell resolution, enabling the identification of disease-driving cell types and genes. However, scRNA-seq remains costly, and there are extremely limited samples generated in even the most extensive human disease studies. In contrast, bulk RNA-seq data is abundant but averages gene expression across all cell types, losing cell-specific detail. To further leverage this abundance of RNA-seq data, methods have been developed to infer cell type proportions and average expression from bulk data using scRNA-seq as a reference. Additionally, generative AI models have been developed to generate more of an existing scRNA-seq dataset, spatial transcriptome data from bulk, and a complete single-cell dataset from bulk, with an incomplete set of single-cell data, for large cohort studies. However, there is a lack of tools specifically dedicated to generating representative single-cell RNA-seq from bulk RNA-seq data. To address this, we develop an innovative, modular framework, termed Bulk2SC, that takes full advantage of powerful generative AI approaches and existing scRNA-seq data to generate representative scRNA-seq data from bulk RNA-seq. Bulk2SC uses a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder for data generation together with any tool that predicts cell type proportions from bulk RNA-seq data. We demonstrate the superior performance of Bulk2SC relative to tools that generate scRNA-seq from bulk RNA-seq as part of broader computational frameworks on published datasets from multiple tissue types. We also apply and assess Bulk2SC on a benchmark deconvolution dataset that contains paired bulk and single nucleus RNA-seq data. The modular design of Bulk2SC allows for deconvolution of single datasets as well as straightforward implementation within larger computational frameworks.

title: Protein sequence domain annotation using a language model
content:
by Arpan Sarkar, Kumaresh Krishnan, Sean R. Eddy

Protein domain annotation underlies large-scale functional inference and is commonly performed by scanning sequences against libraries of profile hidden Markov models (profile HMMs). We describe PSALM, a protein domain annotation method that combines (i) a pretrained protein language model (ESM-2) with (ii) a per-residue domain-state classifier and (iii) a structured probabilistic decoder that produces a single, non-overlapping set of domain calls with explicit boundaries and scores. On a benchmark of 76.9M protein sequences with 107M annotated domains, PSALM attains a domain-detection sensitivity-specificity tradeoff comparable to HMMER. We characterize sequence and residue-level coverage on UniProtKB, observing higher coverage for HMMER at stringent expected false positive counts (E-values) and higher coverage for PSALM at relaxed E-values. We release code for data processing, training, and inference, along with the model weights and datasets used for training, validation, and benchmarking.

title: Biophysically grounded deep learning improves protein–protein ΔΔG prediction
content:
by Jonathan Feldman, Dianzhuo Wang, Antoine Maechler, Eugene I. Shakhnovich

Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in protein–protein binding free energy (ΔΔG) remains limited by small, redundant datasets and train–test homology leakage. We show that commonly used SKEMPI2 splits inflate model performance, with every tested AI predictor declining under a stringent split that controls homology at the level of individual chains (60% sequence identity). We introduce ProtBFF, a modular framework that integrates five residue-level biophysical descriptors into pretrained protein representations through cross-embedding attention. Under leakage-controlled evaluation, ProtBFF improves performance across five sequence- and structure-based encoders. ESM-C achieves the highest Pearson correlation (0.469), while SaProt achieves the highest Spearman correlation (0.437), surpassing specialized ΔΔG predictors. Ablations identify interface features as the dominant contribution and show that pretrained embeddings and biophysical features provide complementary information. ProtBFF also improves low-data transfer to SARS-CoV-2 binding datasets, demonstrating the value of explicit biophysical priors for robust ΔΔG prediction.

title: Systematic clustering alignment and feature characterization for single-cell omics using ACE-OF-Clust
content:
by Xiran Liu, Ritambhara Singh, Sohini Ramachandran

Clustering is widely used to identify cell types in cellular-resolution transcriptomic data, including single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST). Mixed-membership clustering assigns fractional memberships across clusters and captures continuous variation beyond hard clustering, but integrating and interpreting results from either approach is complicated by the “clustering alignment problem,” which arises from label switching, multi-modality, and differences in model settings (including differing numbers of clusters). We introduce ACE-OF-Clust, enabling a four-step workflow for single-cell clustering: multiple clustering, clustering alignment, model comparison, and identification of informative features. ACE-OF-Clust introduces direct comparison of clustering solutions, assesses consistency against annotations, and leverages feature-level clustering profiles to prioritize genes discriminating among cell types, as well as to evaluate how gene sets contribute to clustering patterns. We demonstrate its utility using PBMC scRNA-seq data, breast cancer and mouse embryo ST data, and single-cell multi-omic data. ACE-OF-Clust quantifies cross-omic clustering variability and suggests putative cross-omic regulatory links. Overall, ACE-OF-Clust increases the interpretability, flexibility, and robustness of single-cell clustering, providing a scalable tool for studying cellular heterogeneity and gene expression dynamics.

title: mirCCC: Repression-aware graph learning for miRNA-mediated cell-cell communication inference
content:
by Yifan Chen, Jiaming Cui, Shilong Zhang, Enyan Liu, Luyao Xie, Cong Feng, Ming Chen

Cell-cell communication analyses usually focus on protein ligands and receptors and therefore miss extracellular vesicle transfer of microRNAs, an important route of signalling in cancer. Here we show that microRNA-mediated communication can be inferred from standard single-cell RNA sequencing by detecting coordinated decreases in the expression of validated miRNA target genes. We developed mirCCC, a computational framework that estimates cell-specific microRNA activity, models cellular sending and receiving capacity for extracellular vesicle transfer, and learns microRNA-resolved communication graphs from transcriptomic data. In synthetic benchmarks with strong confounding signals, mirCCC improved whereas all comparison methods declined. Applied to a human colorectal cancer atlas, mirCCC recovered known colorectal cancer-associated microRNAs and identified stromal- and myeloid-to-epithelial communication converging on a plasticity program linked to TGF-β and Wnt/β-catenin signalling. These results provide a practical route for studying extracellular vesicle-mediated communication in existing single-cell atlases.

title: A structure-derived contact-network responsiveness atlas of human proteins
content:
by Ran Huang, Xin Ma, Dean Ta

Protein structures encode non-local contact organization, but static coordinates do not directly quantify how a contact network responds when effective stabilizing interactions are strengthened or weakened. Here we introduce Contact-Network Responsiveness (CNR), a structure-derived framework that converts residue-level protein coordinates into density-controlled and topology-corrected response descriptors. The method is structure-source agnostic and can be applied to experimentally determined PDB structures, AlphaFold models, or other predicted structures; here, human AlphaFold models serve as the high-coverage structural substrate. Across 22,167 valid human protein models, hydrophobic non-local contact density defined a nearly exact Bethe mean-field baseline for the conformational susceptibility threshold. A graph-aware residue-level extension then revealed systematic graph-dependent deviations from this density-only prediction. We define a topology correction ratio, Rtopo=λfGraph/λfBethe, which provides an operational comparison of the two response models; empirical atlas tails define topology-facilitated, density-dominated and topology-suppressed regimes. CNR descriptors were associated with curated DisProt disorder annotations and broad-coverage UniProt/MobiDB-lite disorder fractions, supporting the interpretation that CNR captures a structural organization axis related to non-local contact availability and responsiveness.

title: Social predictability increases with age in dolphins: A marker of longevity?
content:
by Erin R. Siracusa

Social ageing research has focused on changes in average social behaviour, overlooking behavioural consistency as a trait. A new PLOS Biology study shows that wild dolphins’ grouping patterns become more predictable with age, most markedly in the longest-lived animals. Social aging research has focused on age-related changes in behavioral averages, overlooking behavioral consistency as a trait. This Primer explores a new PLOS Biology showing that grouping patterns become more predictable with age in dolphins, and links this pattern to longevity.

title: Correction: Tissue-specific O-GlcNAcylation profiling identifies substrates in translational machinery in Drosophila mushroom body contributing to olfactory learning
High‐Latitude Palaeointensity Data Do Not Support the Geocentric Axial Dipole Hypothesis
content:
Abstract
This study reports 43 new site‐level palaeointensity estimates from Icelandic basalts spanning 2–8 Ma, determined from 880 specimens. These new data significantly increase the number of Icelandic palaeointensity estimates from 2 to 8 Ma. The new estimates are consistent with previously published data and indicate that the geomagnetic field over this interval was persistently weak at high latitudes, with a mean field intensity of 26±11μ $26\pm 11\hspace*{.5em}{\upmu }$T for the new combined Icelandic data set. Incorporating these data into the global palaeointensity database for rocks <8 Ma suggests that the time‐averaged geomagnetic field is not fully described by the geocentric axial dipole hypothesis. Instead, the observed latitudinal variation in palaeointensity requires a persistent non‐dipole contribution of ∼10%. We propose a modification to standard virtual dipole moment calculations that accounts for these non‐dipole field contributions.

title: Enhanced Subsurface Deoxygenation and Nitrate Enrichment in the North Pacific Subtropical Gyre During Recent Decades
content:
Abstract
The North Pacific Ocean has warmed substantially over the past two decades, but the southern subtropical gyre has responded differently amid changes in surface winds and wind‐driven circulation. Long‐term observations from Station ALOHA reveal significant subsurface trends near 450 m on the 26.5 σθ isopycnal, with dissolved oxygen declining by −1.00 ± 0.15 μmol kg−1 yr−1 and nitrate increasing by 0.11 ± 0.03 μmol kg−1 yr−1. In contrast, potential temperature and salinity decline most strongly near 300 m on the shallower 25.4 σθ isopycnal. A Lagrangian advection‐decay model forced by GLORYS12 reanalysis reproduces these observed trends. Model results indicate that anomalous vertical advection drives long‐term changes, while horizontal advection primarily offsets high‐frequency variability. These findings suggest that recent changes in wind‐driven circulation contribute to subsurface deoxygenation and nutrient enrichment, while depth‐dependent differences between the background pycnocline and oxycline/nutricline shape hydrographic and biogeochemical responses.

title: Transforming Critical Water Pipelines Into Seismic Fault Movement Sensors
content:
Abstract
Understanding the influence of fault slip on pipeline deformation at fault‐crossing locations is key to advancing our knowledge of fault movements and protecting critical pipelines. However, the inability to quantify fault movements and associated pipeline deformation makes these key interactions impossible to precisely characterize. To address this gap, we transformed a fiber optic cable‐instrumented pipeline crossing the Hayward Fault near Berkeley, California into a shape sensor. Pipeline deformation and fault movement are directly measured by combining distributed strain and temperature sensing with a Cosserat rod‐based shape reconstruction model. The results precisely capture approximately 4 mm/year of aseismic fault slip. This is the first documented field demonstration of long‐term aseismic fault slip monitoring using distributed fiber optic shape sensing deployed on a pipeline crossing an active fault. This study enables proactive geohazard monitoring by transforming existing pipeline infrastructure into highly sensitive seismic fault sensors.

title: Origins of the North Pacific Meridional Mode Determine Its Distinct Impacts on ENSO
content:
Abstract
The boreal spring North Pacific Meridional Mode (NPMM) has been suggested to influence subsequent El Niño‐Southern Oscillation (ENSO) evolution, but this relationship is unstable. Previous studies attribute the NPMM's origins to multiple atmospheric patterns including the North Pacific Oscillation (NPO), Aleutian Low (AL), and North Pacific Tripole (NPT). Here, we classify the spring NPMM into three types—NPO‐like, AL‐like, and NPT‐like—by applying K‐means clustering to sea level pressure (SLP) anomalies, guided by the recently proposed Hawaiian SLP index. We find that only NPO‐like NPMM events significantly promote subsequent ENSO development. In contrast, AL‐like events are essentially a response to the preceding winter ENSO and do not effectively contribute to ENSO growth, while equatorial coupled conditions in NPT‐like events are unsuitable. These results reconcile the longstanding instability in the NPMM‐ENSO relationship.

title: Transport Dynamics of Droplets Generated by Mechanically Forced Plunging Breaking Waves
content:
Abstract
Residence time is a key input to sea‐spray flux parameterizations and is conventionally estimated assuming droplets settle at their still‐air terminal velocity. Using diameter‐resolved measurements of droplets generated by mechanically forced plunging breaking waves without wind, we show that this assumption fails across most of the measured size range. Small droplets settle up to 1.75 times faster than predicted, while large droplets settle more slowly. We attribute this to wave‐induced oscillatory airflow, which continually accelerates and decelerates small, light droplets as they descend, whereas large droplets are governed by their initial ejection conditions and intermediate droplets exhibit mixed behavior. A Lagrangian transport model, initialized and validated with the measurements, reproduces these dynamics and shows that wave‐induced airflow also governs droplet time of flight and peak height. Residence time formulas should therefore account for these effects where winds are light relative to the breaking wave phase speed.

title: Future Phenology of Chinese Vegetation Is Mediated by Hot Drought Extremes
content:
Abstract
Climate warming is expected to lengthen vegetation growing seasons, but increasing drought and heat may constrain this potential. We derived daily gross primary productivity from a light‐use‐efficiency model driven by multi‐source Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 inputs and projected functional phenology across China under four emissions scenarios. Under SSP5‐8.5, the start of the growing season (SGS) advanced 13.8 days, the end of the growing season (EGS) was delayed 10.9 days, and growing‐season length increased 24.7 days in 2081–2100 relative to 1995–2014. The Joint Drought Indicator (JDI), representing compound soil‐moisture‐temperature exposure, had larger absolute grid‐cell time‐mean coefficients than the Standardized Precipitation‐Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) in 53.06%–63.09% of cells for SGS and 62.97%–69.41% for EGS. However, direct climate variables explained more pooled phenological variation, with temperature and soil moisture contributing most to the pooled SGS and EGS models, respectively. Projected growing‐season extension should be interpreted alongside increasing hot‐drought exposure, particularly in autumn.

title: Disentangling CO2‐Driven Pathways of Future Dryland Change: Contrasting Climate Forcing and Direct Physiological Effects
content:
Abstract
Rising atmospheric CO2 affects drylands through climate forcing and direct physiological effects, but their contributions remain unclear. Using idealized CMIP6 simulations and a modified Penman–Monteith approach incorporating CO2‐induced stomatal regulation, we quantify aridity index changes and dryland redistribution between historical and future periods. Dryland redistribution is substantial, with comparable fractions of global land (∼19%) becoming less or more arid within the dryland domain defined in either period. ∼4% of global land shifts between humid and dryland regimes, while ∼5% transitions among dryland subtypes. Radiative forcing (RAD) is the most widespread dominant pathway, mainly through precipitation‐ and temperature‐mediated effects. At the category‐mean scale, shifts toward more arid conditions are mainly driven by RAD, whereas shifts toward less arid conditions are strongly associated with direct physiological effects. Interactions between RAD and physiological forcing dominate locally through precipitation, relative humidity, and wind speed. These findings advance mechanistic understanding of CO2‐driven dryland redistribution.

title: Agricultural Fallowing Drives Extreme Anthropogenic Dust and Visibility Degradation During the October 2021 Dust Event in California’s Central Valley
content:
Abstract
Anthropogenic dust aerosols from agricultural land affect regional air quality, visibility, and radiation, yet they are often ignored in atmospheric models. Here, we investigate the role of fallow croplands in driving anthropogenic dust emissions during the 11 October 2021, wind‐driven dust event over California’s Central Valley (CV). The simulation without fallow‐cropland erodibility fails to reproduce the dust event, whereas the simulation including it produces 90 t of cumulative dust emissions within the CV, reproducing the observed aerosol optical depth of 0.6–0.8 and PM10 concentrations of 1,000–1,200 μg m−3. Fallow‐cropland‐emitted dust reduces surface net radiation by 30 W m−2, leading to near‐surface cooling of 0.2°C and a model‐diagnosed visibility reduction up to 1,000 m across the CV. These results highlight the important role of agricultural fallowing in regulating regional dust emissions, particularly as climate‐driven drought and groundwater sustainability policy may expand fallowed cropland areas in the coming decades.

title: Increasing Spatial Unevenness of Dry‐Wet Conditions With Global Warming
content:
Abstract
Despite little change in total rainy‐season precipitation across the Northern Hemisphere, extreme dry and wet events have become more frequent, indicating intensifying spatial unevenness of dry‐wet conditions. This observed pattern is consistent with expectations from climate process understanding and evidence from climate models. However, a systematic hemispheric‐scale quantitative assessment of this unevenness remains lacking. To fill this gap, this study examines it through changes in extreme‐event occurrence, distributional shifts, and direct unevenness indices. Observations show that the land area affected by extremes increased by about 1 percentage point per decade, with particularly strong increases in densely populated regions such as the Mediterranean and East Asia. Multi‐model ensemble projections indicate that this tendency will persist and strengthen under higher‐emission scenarios, with increasing divergence toward both drier and wetter extremes. Emission reductions cannot fully prevent this trend but can substantially limit its amplification, highlighting the importance of mitigation and low‐carbon transitions.

title: Two Core Periods of Interdecadal Reduced Summer Precipitation Over the Middle and Lower Yangtze River Basin in the Early 21st Century
content:
Abstract
Summer precipitation over the middle and lower Yangtze River Basin (MLYRB) decreases significantly in the early 21st century compared to the late 20th century. This study reveals that the interdecadal decrease in precipitation over MLYRB in the early 21st century is concentrated in P1 (12–16 June) and P2 (30 June–4 July), with decreases of 4.33 and 6.79 mm/day, respectively. The anomalous divergence in the lower troposphere and anomalous convergence in the upper troposphere over MLYRB during P1 and P2 induce anomalous descending motion and moisture divergence, resulting in negative precipitation anomalies. The reduced precipitation during P1 and P2 is associated with distinct anomalous circulation patterns extending from the North Atlantic to East Asia. Diagnostic analysis and idealized experiments further suggest that warming of sea surface temperature in the northern and western North Atlantic serves as a potential cause of reduced precipitation over MLYRB during P1 and P2, respectively.

title: Particulate Nitrate Photolysis Alters the Atmospheric Chemistry Response to Marine Cloud Brightening Sea Salt Aerosol Emissions
content:
Abstract
Marine cloud brightening (MCB) aims to inject sea salt aerosols (SSA) into the marine boundary layer to increase cloud reflectivity. Limited work has explored how SSA emissions for MCB could impact tropospheric chemistry, and updates to our understanding of MCB and atmospheric chemistry suggest the need for further investigation. Using the 3‐D global atmospheric chemistry model GEOS‐Chem, we explore how a range of SSA emissions scenarios for MCB influence concentrations of tropospheric reactive halogens (Bry, Cly, and Iy) and oxidants (ozone, OH, and NOx), and methane lifetime. Contrary to previous studies, we show enhanced SSA for MCB increases tropospheric oxidant concentrations and shortens methane lifetime (≤15%). Sensitivity simulations demonstrate that increased tropospheric oxidant concentrations and decreased methane lifetime is driven by the treatment of particulate nitrate photolysis. However, the particulate nitrate photolysis mechanism remains poorly constrained, highlighting an important source of uncertainty in evaluating the atmospheric chemistry impacts of MCB.

title: A research agenda for integrating artificial intelligence in mitigation scenario workflows
content:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02801-y

The integration of artificial intelligence into mitigation scenarios development could reduce the current bottlenecks. This Perspective proposes a research agenda to address these challenges at each phase, highlighting the importance of both agentic architecture and expert oversight.

title: Adapting minds to live with climate change
content:
Nature Climate Change, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02804-9

Climate adaptation psychology is fragmented across psychology’s subfields and neighbouring social sciences. This Perspective consolidates the scattered research into a four-layer framework (exposures, mediators, responses and outcomes) and closes with clinical implications and a research agenda.

title: Exchange between ocean and Greenland fjords regulated by recirculating meltwater in glacial troughs
content:
Nature Geoscience, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02147-2

The recirculation of glacial meltwater within a deep Greenland fjord inhibits the inflow of relatively warm ocean water, slowing further glacial melt, according to hydrographic observations and numerical modelling.

content:

This work identifies EpCAM as a marker of fetal-derived alveolar macrophages that supports bacterial uptake. Influenza infection suppresses EpCAM expression on alveolar macrophages, impairing subsequent bacterial clearance and leaving mice more vulnerable to secondary pneumonia.

content:
